articleTitle: A Behavioral Model for Single Leader: Leader-Follower Drone Swarm in Leader’s Failure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The single-leader, leader-follower formation control algorithm is one of the most frequently used formation control approaches in the domain to control drone swarms because of its simple design and overall operational simplicity. However, the major concern faced by such algorithms is the single point of failure problem. This research suggests a distributed leader election approach by incorporating capability-aware measurement to solve the single point of failure problem. The proposed algorithm has three timely bounded phases, and it elects a leader who has the highest capability to be the leader concerning the situation. The performance of the proposed algorithm is assessed using the scenario-based simulations conducted on the SITL simulation environment and showcased the expected behavior from the drone swam in different stages of the simulations.

articleTitle: Comparison of active energy-balance architectures for second-life battery dynamic equalization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The repurposing of exhausted automotive batteries in second-life stationary applications helps to overcome the ethical concerns related to Lithium-Ion battery disposal. However, the aged cells composing second-life batteries present large capacity variability that limits the battery usable energy. The usable energy can be increased using an active balancing architecture implementing dynamic equalization that moves charge from stronger cells to weaker ones during the normal battery operation. However, the high quantity of transferred charge makes the choice of the balancing architecture challenging. This work compares the Direct-Cell-to-Cell, Adjacent-Cell-to-Cell, Cell-to-Pack, and Pack-to-Cell active balancing architectures in different realistic scenarios. Three case studies are analyzed considering Gaussian, Weibull, and bimodal capacity distributions. For each distribution, a Monte Carlo simulation of 10,000 battery modules composed of 10 series-connected cells is carried out. The usable capacity obtained by applying dynamic equalization to each investigated architecture is calculated. The Direct-Cell-to-Cell architecture shows the best performance. However, the large performance gap among the architectures usually found in the literature appears to reduce when realistic scenarios are considered. Therefore, both Adjacent-Cell-to-Cell and Pack-to-Cells architectures emerge as good trade-offs between performance and complexity for dynamic equalization of second-life batteries.

articleTitle: Real-Time Ship Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv8 Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: With the rapid development of marine trade, the demand of ship target detection is increasing. Although there are some existing algorithms, it is difficult to balance the accuracy and real-time performance. Inspired by the YOLOv8n algorithm, we introduce a novel neural network architecture called YOLO-SHIP-DETECTION (YOLO-SD). Based on the YOLOv8n algorithm, YOLO-SD introduces coordinate attention (CA) module, which can capture remote dependencies while retaining accurate position information, thus enhancing the representation of objects of interest. As a result, the accuracy and real-time performance of the model are further improved. By conducting testing on the McShips dataset, YOLOv8n achieves mean average precision (mAP) of 93% with frames per second (FPS) rate of 769.2. Meanwhile, YOLO-SD demonstrates mAP of 93.2% and FPS of 909.1. Our algorithm not only surpasses baseline algorithms but also outperforms numerous contemporary one-stage algorithms.

articleTitle: A Non-Singular Terminal Sliding Mode Control of Buck-Boost Converters Based on Extended State Observer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper focuses on the impact of Buck-Boost converter on the output voltage due to uncertain factors such as output voltage reference changes, load mutations, and input voltage changes. A non-singular terminal sliding mode control method based on an extended state observer (ESO) is proposed. The voltage control loop adopts a non-singular terminal sliding mode control law with an improved sliding mode surface. At the same time, an extended state observer is designed to estimate the uncertainty of the Buck-Boost converter and feed it back to the sliding mode control law, which reduces system chattering and improves system robustness. The simulation results show that the control method proposed in this paper can effectively improve the robustness and response speed of the Buck-Boost converter system.

articleTitle: A non-singular terminal sliding mode control of the DC microgrid with constant power loads
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that constant power load can easily cause DC microgrid bus voltage instability, a non-singular terminal sliding mode control strategy based on an extended state observer is proposed. First, according to the input-output precise feedback linearization theory, the BOOST circuit model is transformed into a Brunovsky standard form linear system, which solves the nonlinear problem caused by the constant power load. Then, a modified sliding mode surface is designed. The non-singular terminal sliding mode control law improves the system convergence speed and reduces system chattering. Considering the external disturbance and uncertainty of the system, an expanded state observer is designed to estimate it, and the estimated value is fed back to the non-singular terminal sliding mode control law, which further reduces the chattering of the system. Finally, based on Lyapunov theory, the stability analysis of the non-singular terminal sliding mode control law is performed. The proposed control strategy ensures that all error signals of the closed-loop system are consistent and ultimately bounded. Simulation results show that the proposed control strategy can effectively improve the response speed and robustness of DC microgrid systems with constant power loads.

articleTitle: SLT-Net: enhanced Mask RCNN network for ship long-tailed detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Significant progress has been made in class-balanced benchmarks for ship detection. Nonetheless, their performance in real-world scenarios is subpar, even falling short of expectations. This is primarily attributed to the long-tailed distribution of categories. To address the aforementioned challenges, this paper proposes a ship long-tailed network, named SLT-Net, for fine-grained detection of ships in optical remote sensing images. In particular, SLT-Net employs ResLT as the backbone network, combined with Mutual Information (MI) Loss to enhance the detection performance. Firstly, ResLT takes into account the parameter space and aims to reserve specific capacity for tail classes, thereby rebalancing the representation of head and tail classes. Then, MI Loss, instead of Cross-Entropy, is employed to minimize the discrepancy between the real probability distribution and the predicted probability distribution by fitting mutual information. Experimental results on the ShipRSImageNet dataset demonstrate that SLT-Net outperforms existing SOTA networks, showcasing the best performance in terms of ship detection.

articleTitle: High-precision Trajectory Tracking Control for Uncertain Nonminimum Phase Hypersonic Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Hypersonic vehicle (HSV) is one of the cutting-edge technologies in the research area of aerospace and is also an intensively focused strategic direction for global military powers. Precise prompt global strike as the ultimate skill of HSV, the key relies on high-precision trajectory tracking control. Due to the lack of experimental data, the accurate model of an HSV is very difficult to obtain. Besides, the HSV model exhibits nonminimum phase property. These features make it extremely difficult to achieve high-precision trajectory tracking control for an HSV, which has become a bottleneck for the development of the HSV control system. To this end, this paper focuses on high-precision trajectory tracking control for a nonminimum phase HSV, with special emphasis on the existence of model uncertainties. The proposed control framework consists of three parts. Firstly, design of a minimum-phase new output based on virtual constraints and robust optimization. Secondly, calculation of the ideal internal dynamics based on experience replay and optimal bounded inversion. Thirdly, robust nonlinear controller design based on receding horizon. By the end of this research, a control framework is built for high-precision trajectory tracking for nonminimum phase HSVs, which can provide scientific theory and support for the sustainable development of the HSV control technology.

articleTitle: Event-triggered control for fuzzy Markov jump systems with deception attack
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this study, we focus on the deception attack-based output-feedback control for fuzzy Markov jump systems with an event-triggered protocol. It should be noted that deception attack is described by a Bernoulli process and is assumed to cause the output feedback signal to be altered. In order to improve resource utilization and control performance, reduce communication burden, an event-triggered protocol is proposed. Additionally, in unreliable networks, phenomena such as data transmission might experience delays. Therefore, a time-delay system is considered in this study. Then, a hidden-Markov-model-based asynchronous fuzzy controller is designed since the controller may not have full access to the mode information of the system. A parameter-dependent Lyapunov function is introduced to ensure the stochastic stability of the closed-loop system. Finally, a numerical example is designed to testify the effectiveness of the presented approach.

articleTitle: Enhanced Data Acquisition System of Current Signature for Diagnosis of Variable Speed Induction Motor Drives with Full ADC Range Utilization and Noise Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The effective and dependable performance of variable-speed induction motor drives is of utmost importance across a wide range of industrial applications. The early identification of prospective issues and declines in system performance is vital for maintaining seamless operations. This paper presents an enhanced data acquisition system designed to capture and analyze the current signature of variable-speed induction motors with a focus on optimizing data quality and diagnostic accuracy. The proposed system employs a comprehensive approach that introduces the Optimized Common Mode Signal Clamping to use single ended Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) effectively. Following this, the Auto Gain Adjuster is employed for full ADC range utilization. The Auto Gain Adjuster not only enhances the targeted signal but also magnifies associated noise with it. By utilizing advanced noise cancellation techniques and signal conditioning, the system enhances the accuracy of current signature analysis for motor health diagnosis.

articleTitle: A flexible, highly sensitivity and wideband width response non-contact triboelectric nanogenerator for online vibration monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) have attracted much attention as a promising energy harvesting and self-powered sensing method. In this study, we developed a flexible, highly sensitive and wideband wide response non-contact TENG for on-line vibration detection. FEP and PI have excellent charge transfer capacity, charge adsorption capacity and chemical stability, so we chose them as the friction layer for assembling the TENG. The contactless TENG demonstrates excellent flexibility and stability, so it can be applied as a shape adaptive device to uneven device surfaces. The response sensitivity at different distances is studied. When the distance between two friction layers is increased at fixed vibration frequency, the response sensitivity is 2.586 Vmm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> for 1 mm-1.1 mm, 1.201 Vmm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> for 1.1 mm-2 mm, and 0.306 Vmm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> for 2 mm-3 mm respectively. In addition, we can detect vibration signals of different frequencies (1 Hz-400 Hz) without contact. Therefore, the fault information of non-planar mechanical equipment can be collected in a lossless state. Finally, the TENG is applied to the on-line vibration monitoring of the equipment in working state. This work demonstrates the TENG's potential for non-contact and non-destructive detection of mechanical devices with irregular surfaces.

articleTitle: Cybersecurity Vulnerabilities in Phase-Locked Loop (PLL) of DFIG-Based Wind Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The integration of wind energy, particularly Doubly-Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) turbines, into power grids has increased significantly owing to their performance and cost-efficiency. Within the DFIG-based turbines, a critical component is the Phase-Locked Loop (PLL). This study delves into the cybersecurity vulnerabilities associated with PLL systems. Initially, a dynamic model for DFIG turbines—including voltage and current control loops and the PLL—is developed. The PLL model is assumed to work based on the fundamental frequency of the positive sequence of voltage. Then, it has been shown that when a malicious signal with the natural frequency of PLL is injected into the measurements, the estimation of phase angle will start to oscillate. This instability, in turn, leads to disruptions in the stability of the active power injected into the grid which results in DFIG disconnection and highly threatens the grid stability. We further investigate the impacts of the proposed attack under varying parameter configurations, employing the EPRI benchmark within the EMTP-RV software.

articleTitle: Static and Dynamic Memory Protection using Type-Based Memory Layout in Rust
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Hardware supported memory protection is a commonly adopted approach to runtime verification of memory accesses. However, protection is typically coarse grained where trusted drivers and kernel code is given access to unnecessarily large portions of the memory space. This approach implies huge costs to verification, validation and certification of trusted code.In this paper we propose an alternative approach, leveraging on memory safety guarantees of the Rust systems level programming language together with a novel type-based method to statically determine the memory layout of the application. The memory layout information can be used for further static code analysis, proving access pattern properties, and is used as an outset for fine grained hardware supported memory protection.While the proposed approach is novel and breaks with traditional and industrial practice, our results are applicable to existing hardware platforms and holds the potential to provide leap-step improvements to safety and security of embedded devices.

articleTitle: A Digital Twin-Oriented Data Link Modeling System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The research on data link system has attracted more and more attention. The accuracy of the models is a vital prerequisite for effective research. Hence, there is an urgent need for a new data link modeling approach to enhance the correctness and comprehensiveness of data link models. Different from traditional data link modeling in simulations, this paper presents a data link modeling approach based on digital twin technology. It analyzes the functional architecture of this system and concludes by summarizing the advantages and future directions of this system.

articleTitle: Detection and Mitigation of False Data Injection Attacks on Wide Area Damping Controllers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In modern cyber-physical power systems (CPPSs), wide-area damping controls (WADCs) are responsible for damping the oscillations and improving stability. The deployment of such a wide area control scheme requires a significant amount of cyber systems, which makes the entire grid prone to a variety of cyber-attacks, e.g., false data injection attacks (FDIAs). On this basis, this paper proposes a coordinated approach for enhancing the resilience of WADCs against FDIAs. Initially, a detection technique employing a deep neural network (DNN) is employed to identify the FDIAs on WADC. Subsequently, a mitigation strategy is developed by utilizing an interval type-2 Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy control to mitigate the attack. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodologies compared to the conventional approaches.

articleTitle: Improving the Resilience of Modular Multilevel Converters using Concurrent Estimators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Due to the widespread employment of power electronic devices with complex and occasionally remote/cloud control or monitoring in the future power systems, their secure operation would play a significant role in the resilient supply of critical loads. The modular multilevel converter (MMC) is a well-established topology in high and medium voltage levels due to its inherent redundancy and numerous technical advantages. This study investigates the operation of MMCs under false data injection attacks (FDIA) and proposes a practical solution for detecting and mitigating them. We propose to employ two concurrent estimators, module level and arm level using Kalman filter and neural networks, in order to improve the resilience of the MMC and compensate for the shortcomings of the detection methods presented in the literature against sophisticated attacks. The simulation study clearly proves the feasibility of the proposed dual estimator technique, and thus its contribution to improving the cyber resilience of MMCs.

articleTitle: Multivalued attribute encoding and feature generating for zero-shot diagnosis of machine faults
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This study addresses a machine fault diagnosis task in which the model is trained without any samples, specifically those involving the monitoring of sensor signals related to the target faults. Recognizing that attributes or semantic descriptions of the unseen faults might be available in advance, this study employs zero-shot learning (ZSL) techniques, which have their origins in the field of computer vision, to tackle the challenge of zero-sample fault diagnosis of mechanical systems. To enhance the representation of fault semantic information, a multivalued encoding approach is employed. This method allows for the expression of both the presence and absence of attributes, as well as the strength of these attributes. As a result, it provides a more comprehensive and nuanced understanding of machine fault characteristics. Building upon this attribute encoding approach, a zero-shot fault diagnosis model is established by utilizing an attribute conditional feature generating adversarial network. The results obtained unequivocally demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits competitive performance when compared to state-of-the-art zero-shot learning algorithms. This underscores the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach in the zero-shot fault diagnosis of mechanical systems.

articleTitle: DC Link Voltage Optimization for Efficiency Enhancement of Electric Vehicle Onboard Chargers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are becoming increasingly popular, so it is important to study the efficiency of the EV onboard charging (OBC) systems comprehensively. This paper is focused on the DC link voltage optimization to enhance the overall grid to vehicle (G2V) charging efficiency of the OBC. An EV OBC with ac-dc power factor correction (PFC) and dc-dc dual active bridge (DAB) stages is studied, where the power losses for various converter components are formulated as functions of DC link voltage, battery voltage, and charging power. Afterwards, the optimal DC link voltages corresponding to the minimum total loss at different charging conditions are obtained from theoretical analysis of the circuit for both level-1 and level-2 chargers. A 500 W OBC prototype is experimented in two cases, and the results show that the optimal DC link selection of 345V yields to an overall efficiency improvement of 2% compared to the fixed DC link design (at 400V), while the PFC and DAB stage efficiencies are individually improved and declined by 2.6% and 0.5%, respectively.

articleTitle: Hybrid battery model parameter estimation and optimization using a two-step procedure and parameter sensitivity analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper presents an effective and simple approach for parameter estimation and optimization of a simplified first principle (SFP) model of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). Unlike existing parameter estimation and optimization methods, this proposed approach first decouples and estimates some key parameters based on theoretical analysis and experimental data. In order to alleviate the influence of the previous parameter estimation steps on the subsequent ones, and reduce parameter optimization cost, it conducts parameter sensitivity analysis with SFP model to study the parameter identifiability, and sets parameters with low identifiability to fix values. Then it utilizes particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm to optimize parameters with high identifiability. The proposed approach is validated with experimental data under a dynamic loading profile. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach using a two-step procedure can effectively and accurately identify parameters of SFP model to simulate dynamic behaviors of LIBs, providing a reliable foundation for the development of model-based battery management systems.

articleTitle: The Obstacle Avoidance Pursuit-Evasion Game with A Non-Quadratic Performance Index Based on Polynomial Approximation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this paper, the pursuit-evasion problem under obstacle environment between two wheeled robots is investigated by the Stackelberg game. To address this problem, a linear non-quadratic differential game theorem with the general form is proposed, supplying a unified framework to obtain the analytical nonlinear control strategies. The Lyapunov function with a similar non-quadratic form, as the solution to the Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs equation, is designed by polynomial approximation methods. Therefore, Stackelberg Equilibrium (SE) can be reached and the stability is guaranteed with the closed-loop feedback control laws. The experiments on two wheeled robots demonstrate the effectiveness of the SE strategies.

articleTitle: Voltage Regulation of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator in Variable Load by Using Buck-Converter in Aircraft Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Generator drive applications have been used in many different systems for a long time. There are plenty of different kinds of generators and generator control topologies. One of the generator control topologies is the DC-DC buck converter. So, implementing a buck converter topology to generator control makes the design simple, efficient and easy to apply. This paper presents a control application of a 15kW permanent magnet synchronous generator by using a buck converter in aircraft applications. This application involves new technologies such as Silicon Carbide and environmentally reliable components. According to the theoretical calculations, the selected components for practical implementation are given. The losses of selected semiconductors and passive components are calculated individually. At the end of the paper, the theoretical calculation and simulation results are compared with the experimental results.

articleTitle: A Novel E/F Contoller for Squirrel Cage Induction Motor Based on Rotor Flux Orientation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this paper, a novel E/F controller is proposed for three phase squirrel cage induction machine based on its rotor flux oriented model. The proposed controller is intended for a current sensor-less induction motor drive operating with speed feedback and it offers an attractive solution to various problems associated with the conventional V/F type of controller. The speed control loop of the proposed controller emulates the back emf of the motor and not the terminal voltage and therefore, the reduction in magnetizing flux in the low speed region is overcome. In addition, the zero speed operation becomes feasible in the proposed E/F controller which is difficult to realize in case of conventional V/F controller. Moreover, since the proposed controller is based on the rotor flux oriented model of the motor, it gives a performance which is on par with a vector controlled drive and the control algorithm is simplified to a greater extent. The proposed controller is validated through simulation. To highlight its performance, it is also compared with conventional vector drive.

articleTitle: A Stable Control Method Designing for Longitudinal Platoon Problems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a neural network architecture that guarantees stability and applies it to address the longitudinal vehicle platoon problem. Considering the safety and consistency requirements during the operation of the platoon, traditional neural network algorithms struggle to meet the stability requirements. To address this issue, this paper introduces a control framework, i.e., QRNET, that combines the Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) and Neural Network (NN). QRNET ensures asymptotic stability at least near the equilibrium point and improves the problem-solving dimensionality. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed neural network architecture ensures stability and satisfactory dynamic performance of the longitudinal vehicle platoon.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Voltage Control Methods for Single-Phase Grid-Forming Inverters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This work compares three types of control-loop implementation for single-phase grid-forming inverters. The first two follow a single-loop approach using proportional resonant (PR) controllers in the Natural Reference Frame and proportional integral controllers in the synchronous reference (SRF-PI). The third control loop is also based on an SRF-PI controller. However, it has two loops, where the innermost one is related to the current that passes through the filter capacitor, and the outermost one is related to the inverter voltage. The article employs a simulation methodology to analyze the dynamic behavior of the control loops. In the established environments, it was shown that systems in SRF present a better transient response to step changes in the reference value. Furthermore, all three systems achieve zero error at steady state conditions.

articleTitle: A Deep Double-Convolutional Neural Network-Based Fault Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Fault detection is crucial for saving valuable maintenance time and costs of industrial systems when faults occur. Faults are usually cataloged into sudden faults and degraded faults, which have diverse impacts on system safety. So, distinct treatment should be treated during fault detection. In this paper, an intelligent fault detection method is proposed based on a double-convolutional neural network (CNN) model architecture to detect whether faults occur and which type they belong. Firstly, a CNN model is employed to judge whether faults occur. Furthermore, the "Majority rule" is applied to effectively eliminate the influence of outliers for enhancing the robustness of fault detection model. Then, Another CNN model combined with root-mean-square (RMS) is introduced to detect fault types that belong to the sudden fault or degraded fault. Finally, an experimental study involving four types of bearing degradation scenarios is conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Gate-Driving Technique for Enhancing the GaN Power Transistors Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of a gate-driving technique for enhancing the switching performance of gallium nitride (GaN) power transistors. The technique consists of modifying the Pulse Width Modulated (PWM) signal that is applied to the gate of transistors by using diodes and a totem pole circuit. As purpose of this technique is to control the turn-on and turnoff HEMT GaN transitions and reduce the oscillations caused by high-speed operation without increasing power losses. LTsipice is used for analyzing the gate driving technique by simulations considering models of commercial components. Simulation results show the viability of the proposed, which can reduce the ringing in the GaN transitions without affecting their performance.

articleTitle: An improved cross-entropy method for the water pump scheduling optimization problem
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The growing demand for urban freshwater supply often corresponds to rising electrical and labor costs for pump stations. Optimizing the operation of water pumps, ensuring they run at their most efficient working points, and improving their scheduling systems offer effective ways to mitigate costs and conserve water resources. These water pump stations and their associated systems can be mathematically modeled, enabling the use of optimization algorithms to assess optimal operating conditions. Conventional optimization methods often fall short when dealing with such complex models, underscoring the significance of investigating recent algorithms. In this study, we expand the research on the cross-entropy method and introduce an improved version to address water pump scheduling optimization. Notable enhancements include an improved update step for the multivariate normal distribution used in sampling, resulting in faster and more accurate outcomes, as well as reduced susceptibility to local minima. Moreover, our adaptive objective function takes into account various cost factors and penalty functions associated with complex constraints, with the primary aim of further minimizing power consumption costs. To validate our approach, we conducted a series of experiments within a simulated environment and on a real-life-inspired scenario modeled after a water pump station located in Shanghai. The results of these experiments demonstrate the adaptability of our optimization method to complex models and constraints and highlight its satisfactory performance outcomes.

articleTitle: Wind power model-based control strategies for green energy generation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Wind power is a great alternative in the search for clean and green energy sources, especially for green and emerging countries. With the aim of reducing the costs of the control system in wind farms and guaranteeing their viability, this work proposes a non-linear model for a 5 MW wind turbine, that was compared to an existing data model of a real turbine, and it represents the turbine’s behavior with sufficient fidelity but reducing complexity. Moreover, it is shown through numerical results how to apply simple and advanced model-based control strategies, that are beneficial to the wind turbine in terms of robustness and performance. Also, predictive and PID controllers show that both methods are promising optimal control strategies under stochastic wind speed disturbances.

articleTitle: A Design and Implementation of a Novel Multi-Stage Ultra High Gain DC-DC Converter with Boost Cell Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel multi-stage ultrahigh gain DC-DC converter featuring a minimal component count, including a single semiconductor switch. This converter achieves substantial voltage gain even at lower duty ratios, effectively reducing voltage stress on both the switch and diodes. The proposed converter leverages two distinct boost cell configurations, namely the 2LC2D and C2D designs. The 2LC2D boost cell consists of two inductors, one capacitor, and two diodes, collectively forming an active switched inductor capacitor network (SLCN). On the other hand, the C2D boost cell comprises one capacitor and two diodes. The paper primarily investigates the converter’s performance within the context of an n-stage SLCN converter, with a particular focus on the fundamental stage. Its compact design renders it well-suited for various applications, including renewable energy, electric vehicles, and fuel cells. The paper provides a comprehensive explanation of the working principle and steady-state analysis, accompanied by simulation results that substantiate the theoretical findings. This innovative converter demonstrates exceptional performance characteristics and exhibits significant potential across a wide spectrum of applications.

articleTitle: An Improved VFH+ Algorithm for Real-time Obstacle Avoidance in Unmanned Surface Vessel
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: At present, the marine field is receiving more and more attention, and the path planning capability of unmanned surface vessels is of paramount importance. This capability allows these vessels to avoid obstacles and successfully reach their intended destinations. Path planning can be categorized into global and local planning. In the face of complex and changeable maritime environment, this paper proposes an improved VFH+ algorithm which aims at local planning and real-time obstacle avoidance ability. The performance and obstacle avoidance success rate of the algorithm are improved in three key ways: (1) By considering the movement characteristics of the specific used unmanned vessel, the range of selectable directions is ameliorated; (2) Refining the cost formula for direction choice aids in addressing the "dead end" issue; and (3) The path point generation strategy is optimized by using the eband-planner for smoother obstacle avoidance. The efficacy of these enhancements is corroborated through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: A quasi-differential type event-triggered MPC for non-holonomic robots with coupled constraints and bounded disturbances
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: A new event-triggered model predictive control (MPC) strategy is conceived in this paper for non-holonomic robot systems. This strategy is different from traditional event-triggered schemes that only consider the actual state and optimal prediction error at a single moment. When designing the proposed triggering condition, the so-called quasi-differential information of continuous state errors is considered to reduce the frequency of solving optimization problems and data transmission. Furthermore, an exponential robustness state constraint is considered in designing the optimal control problem to accelerate the convergence speed of mobile robots toward the desired path. Sufficient conditions are provided to guarantee stability of the non-holonomic system. Finally, a simulation comparison is used to verify the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Research on Formation Control for Unmanned Surface System Based on Behavioral Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Facing the complex environment of surface and underwater, unmanned surface system cluster is the key research direction of future military unmanned system equipment. In this paper, simulation modeling is carried out for the unmanned surface system formation based on the behavioral approach, pre-defined the change of unmanned surface system from an aggregated state to a formation of 4 rows and 4 columns on the water surface, the definition of sensor ranges for unmanned surface system and the study of following algorithms, the sensor model and destruction model of the unmanned surface equipment are established, the initial formation position and tracking adsorption behavior of the surface unmanned equipment are established, and the feasibility of this formation control is verified.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Photovoltaic and Battery System with Maximum-Power-Point Tracking and Load Sharing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The increasing global demand for renewable energy sources, particularly solar photovoltaic (PV) power, highlights the need for efficient energy storage solutions and improved system stability. This paper presents a novel approach to solve these challenges through a reconfigurable PV and battery hybrid control platform based on modular multilevel series/parallel technology. The proposed system enables coordinated operation of PV and battery sources within a single system, offering enhanced flexibility and improved energy utilization. By employing a flexible configuration of PV and battery modules, the system optimizes power generation by ensuring each PV operates at its maximum power point for as long as possible, while mitigating the negative effects of rigid connections. The battery module seamlessly adapts to PV output and load fluctuations, ensuring stable output at the DC bus voltage. Moreover, the integration of balancing chokes minimizes current fluctuations caused by sudden voltage changes. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed topology and control strategy, demonstrating its ability to meet system operation requirements.

articleTitle: Optimizing Transfer Efficiency in Multi-Cloud Storage Systems with Edge and Fog Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Multi-cloud environments have emerged as a promising solution for computing, offering scalability, fault tolerance, and vendor flexibility. However, efficient data transfer between multiple cloud providers and data owners is crucial for ensuring optimal performance and timely execution of workloads. This paper explores the challenges associated with data transfer rates in multi-cloud storage systems and discusses various optimization strategies to improve data transfer efficiency. It highlights the limitations of single-cloud storage systems and the unresolved issues related to data transfer in conventional models. To address these challenges, a comprehensive architecture is proposed, integrating multiple cloud storage services and leveraging fog and edge computing paradigms. The study aims to optimize the data transfer efficiency in multi-cloud storage systems.

articleTitle: Control of Parallel Buckboost Converters in a Microgrid using an Extended Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: A control scheme for a system of parallel connected buckboost converters in a microgrid is proposed in this paper. The paralleled converters supply an instantaneous constant power load (CPL). An Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) based control scheme is designed to minimize the number of state variables measured. The output voltage of the paralleled converters is the only state variable that is measured and the other state variables are estimated using EKF. The EKF based state estimates quickly converge to the actual converter state variables both in open loop and closed loop. The proposed state estimator based controller is implemented in the form of two control loops namely an inner and an outer loop. The droop based inner control loop performs current sharing and damps limit cycle oscillations due to CPL. An integral controller based outer loop is added to enable voltage regulation without affecting current sharing. Stability conditions for equilibrium point are obtained. Simulation results are presented to show the validity of the proposed control approach.

articleTitle: A Novel Input-Parallel Output-Series SEPIC-Cuk Converter for Bipolar Voltage Balancing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This article describes a novel Input-Parallel Output-Series SEPIC-Cuk (IPOSSC) converter formulated for application in low voltage bipolar DC microgrid (BDMG) systems. The proposed bi-directional converter adopts a single input dual output configuration with inherited common ground and employs an interleaved-structure to reduce source current fluctuations when linked to sustainable energy sources (SES) such as solar PV or energy storage elements (ESE) like batteries. The article includes the development of a dynamic model for this proposed circuit and formulates closed-loop controller for precise current and voltage regulation. Additionally, by integrating dispatchable sources like a battery into the source terminals, the IPOSSC can operate in voltage regulation mode to effectively control the bus voltage. Furthermore, the article explores an intriguing approach to counteract voltage unbalance in BDMG systems without relying on an active energy source connected to the source terminal. It harnesses the IPOSSC capabilities as a DC compensator, similar to an active shunt filter or D-STATCOM in AC systems, with the converter only incurring losses and not supplying or consuming power. The article substantiates the efficacy of the IPOSSC converter through simulation results depicting its performance in various operating modes.

articleTitle: An Insecticidal Counting Method Based on Insecticidal Discharge Sound Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The Solar Insecticidal Lamp is a low-carbon, green physical plant protection device. Its nightly kill count can be used to measure the density of the insect population in farmland areas to control the occurrence of insect pests. Aiming to address the issue of repetitive counting associated with existing voltage-based methods, a technique for insecticidal counting based on the time domain analysis of insecticidal discharge sound is proposed. This method resolves the problem of repeated counting, and the equipment used is simple, making it suitable for use with the insecticidal lamp. In the optimal solution, the overall accuracy of insecticide counting is 97.60%, and the accuracy of correctly distinguishing the number of single kills is 83.25%. Compared with the traditional voltage counting method, the former’s accuracy is improved by 14.9%, and the latter’s accuracy is improved by 37.25%. The results indicate that using this method to count the number of insecticides improves the accuracy of insecticidal counting and provides a more robust basis for pest control.

articleTitle: An Optical Artificial Skin for Pressure Point Localisation on Robotic Arm Links
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper presents the development and evaluation of an optical artificial skin capable of accurately measuring contact location and pressure. The artificial skin consists of a flexible transparent gel that is wrapped around on a cylinder such that it can cover robotic arms and prostheses. The setup incorporates pairs of phototransistors and light emitting diodes placed at opposite ends of the cylindrical structure. The investigation uses white and infrared light sources and two types of contact point shapes. The data capturing is automated to improve efficiency and reduce errors. Neural Networks are employed to capture the physics of light propagation in the gel material. Using white light, the system achieves a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 2.7 cm in determining the contact point position, correctly identifies the contact point shape 95.2% of the time and correctly classifies the pressure level 88.5% of the time. With infrared light, the RMSE for the contact point position is 3.65 cm, the contact point shape is identified correctly 96% of the time, and pressure level classification is correct 85.6% of the time.

articleTitle: Design And Development Of A High-Performance Current Trasnformer For Switchgear Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of a high-performance Current Transformer (CT) tailored for switchgear applications. CTs play a critical role in sensing currents and powering up Electronic trip units (ETU), ensuring effective operation of circuit breakers. Our research focuses on meeting two primary objectives. The first is to power up the trip unit and second is to accurately sense primary currents over a specified range while minimizing metering errors. To achieve these goals, we employed advanced design principles and optimum choice of materials in the construction of the CT. The resulting CT prototype demonstrates exceptional performance in terms of early power up of ETU, rapid saturation, and precise current measurement, making it an ideal choice for modern circuit breakers and other applications in the power industry.

articleTitle: Grid Interactive PV-fed BLDC Motor with Power Quality Features using Predictive Current Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Renewable energy features have contributed to the popularity of solar Photo Voltaic (PV) in recent decades, which can operate in grid-connected mode or islanded mode with energy storage systems. The expected features of the controller are to provide reliable power even under high-fidelity dynamic conditions. In this paper, a grid-interactive solar PV-fed Brushless Direct Current (BLDC) motor water pump is implemented, using a non-linear model predictive current controller. Additionally, power quality features are included in PV DC-DC converters and grid-side three-phase voltage source inverters (TPVSI). It is not recommended to use linear control structures that operate at a single operating point, such as Proportional Integral (PI) controllers. Also, under dynamic load conditions; such as sudden changes in DC loads, starting of BLDC motor, sudden load applied or removed from the motor pump, and changes in linear or non-linear loads applied at Point of Common Coupling (PCC). Therefore, a proper control scheme is required to alleviate these challenges. A grid-interactive solar PV-fed BLDC motor with a non-linear-based model predictive controller is required. The proposed predictive controller helps to achieve (i) better dynamics during the sudden changes, (ii) unity power factor on the grid side despite non-linear loads being connected, and (iii) the PV panel operates at its maximum power point under all conditions. The proposed model predictive controller with solar pump is validated through MATLAB/SIMULINK and results are presented.

articleTitle: Visualization of the outliers detected by the SLAMICP library
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: During the navigation of a mobile robot in an unconstrained environment, unexpected objects may appear that block the planned path of the robot. Detecting and identifying these obstacles is key to avoiding possible crashes. The SLAMICP library provides efficient computation of the location of the robot while simultaneously identifying outlier points in a LiDAR scan, which enables higher data throughput. This paper evaluates the obstacle detection capabilities offered by the outlier detection feature of the SLAMICP library. Various test obstacles have been used to assess the ability of the library to differentiate elements that are not part of the original mapped area. These test objects include different boxes representing static obstacles and a walking person as a dynamic obstacle. The results show that all test objects were successfully detected and located within the map. The shape of the static obstacles was reconstructed by adding together the location of the outliers across multiple scans. Using the same method with the dynamic obstacle revealed the trajectory of the walking person.

articleTitle: A Comparison Track of Bearingless Double U-core Switched Reluctance Machine Considering 3 & 4 Double U-cores
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This study has explored the pattern of even and odd stator coils in bearingless double u-core switched reluctance machine (bearingless double u-core SRM) and examined their effects in the bearingless control strategy. In this investigation, the currents in the stator coils have the responsibility for holding the rotor in the center and controlling the airgap simultaneously with producing the torque and rotating the machine. This approach brings considerable interest in the future for the control system of bearingless SRMs by suspension manipulating using torque generating coils, without having any friction and erosion. To assess the behaviour of the bearingless double u-core SRM, dynamic model of the machine is evaluated under the same conditions for two different scenarios of three and four double u-cores in the stator structure. The results are stated in terms of implications of achieving the desired speed, possessing maximum force in the x- and y- direction and detecting airgap displacement while minimizing eccentricity.

articleTitle: An Investigation of Direct and Indirect Powers of DC-DC Conversion Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The theory describing the fundamental limits on DC-DC conversion systems as first proposed by Wolaver is gaining popularity as it is applied in many situations to reduce loss in DC-DC converters. However there are some inconsistencies in the theory’s predictions. This study applies Wolaver’s theory to both a conventional boost converter and a full bridge in a partial power processing DC-DC conversion architecture. These two converters are shown to have the same predicted direct and indirect powers as they are topologically equivalent. However when simple loss models are incorporated into the analysis, the two converters show different behaviors in the direct and indirect path efficiencies. The partial power processor matches well with the theory but the conventional boost converter does not. The main reason for the breakdown in the theory is the difference between the operational and averaged waveforms of the converters. This leads to the conclusion that while the theory of the fundamental limits is sound, it’s application needs careful consideration.

articleTitle: Single DC Source Based Asymmetric Multilevel Inverter : Principle, Modulation And Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: A single DC source-based asymmetric multilevel inverter is presented in this paper. The auxiliary dc sources of the proposed converter are replaced by floating capacitors using Level Doubling Network (LDN) principle. These capacitors do not require closed-loop control and naturally converge to the desired voltage in steady-state operation. The highest voltage bridge is supplied by the DC source, and all three bridges maintain a binary ratio of asymmetry. A combination of half-bridge and full-bridge LDNs are used to reduce the switch count with some reasonable trade-off in output voltage levels. Half-bridge LDNs are merged together to reduce the capacitor requirement further. Concept of the natural convergence of capacitor voltages and modulation technique is explained in details. Simulations of the proposed converter is carried out using MATLAB/SIMULINK. Simulation results matched well with theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Design and Control of Ant3DBot: A Modular Self-Reconfigurable Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative modular self-reconfigurable robot named Ant3DBot, aiming to address the limitations of existing self-reconfigurable robots. Combining the advantages of wheeled and legged robots, Ant3DBot comprises four iron spheroid shells, telescopic legs, and internal magnets that can rotate around the center. Through a single motor, synchronous belt, and compressed springs, it can expand its shells and legs, forming distinct docking states. Moreover, the robot is equipped with multiple connector configurations, allowing it to operate flexibly in diverse environments. In its expanded state, Ant3DBot can easily traverse obstacles up to 8 cm in height and pass through an outdoor 25° slope. For unstructured environments, multiple Ant3DBots can collaborate, reaching target points through simple control. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that Ant3DBot performs remarkably, whether operating singly or in collaborative modes, accomplishing a variety of complex tasks, showcasing its excellent mobility and versatility.

articleTitle: Multiple Markov chains-based layered random fault injection method for the air braking system
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The air braking system is one of the key systems to ensure the safe operation of high-speed trains, and it’s also one of the most frequent sources of fault. In order to achieve the requirements of low risk, low cost and short cycle in the research, fault injection is often carried out in the form of simulation. Due to the random occurrence of faults in the system, random fault injection can simulate the scenario of fault occurrence more realistically than deterministic fault injection. However, the challenges are the lack of raw fault data for the air braking systems and the process of building the fault distribution function is too cumbersome. This paper proposes a layered random fault injection method based on multiple Markov chains (MCs). First, a multi-layer structure fault model base is established for the system, and layered fault injection is performed. On this basis, the fault type and fault degree Markov chains are constructed, the state transition matrix is constructed, and the steady-state probability distribution is solved by using the steady-state property of the Markov chain to obtain the fault probability distribution. Then, a low-complexity Alias Sampling algorithm is used for discrete random sampling, and the normal model is transformed into a corresponding fault model according to the sampling results to obtain fault data.

articleTitle: A Linear Observer Design for Fast Open Switch Fault Detection of Interleaved Boost Converters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a fault detection, identification, and reconfiguration approach for an open switch fault (OCF)for the interleaved DC-DC boost converter (IBC). The proposed technique is based on a state space observer nonlinear model with a linear design. The main idea is based on evaluating the residual vector created by comparing the real and the estimated inductor phase currents. The chosen observer model with the linear design and the adopted control system of the IBC will result in a very fast fault detection time using just the sensed variables of the circuit. Moreover, a thresholding strategy is adopted and tested under several conditions to avoid false diagnosis cases. The effectiveness of the proposed method for one or more open switch faults has been verified by simulation for three and five interleaved boost converters.

articleTitle: A High-Speed Current Regulator Based on a Buck DC-DC Converter Using a Direct Deadbeat Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The paper presents analysis and design of a high-speed current regulator based on a buck DC-DC converter using a direct deadbeat control technique. The large signal mathematical model of the closed-loop current regulating system is developed in the form of nonlinear difference equations. The results of computational experiment obtained for dynamical operation mode under large disturbances at the source and load sides show a high efficiency of the proposed control method.

articleTitle: Development of a system for measuring teacher movements using a laser distance sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Different characteristics were found in individual check individually by making our rounds in the classroom between Skilled teachers and inexperienced teachers. Skilled teachers are taking a view from multiple items such as learner and learner’s materials. On the other hand, It is suggested that those with no teaching experience are not able to see from multiple items. These surveys are based on analysis of video recordings, and the results cannot be said to be the same for everyone. A case study of quantitative analysis of check individually by making our rounds in the classroom and a method using RFID tags is reported. In this method, RFID tags are placed every in the classroom aisles to obtain the location information of the teacher. However, it is difficult to install sensors. In this research, we focused on laser range sensor mounted on robots and other devices. The goal is to develop a system for analyzing check individually by making our rounds in the classroom with a single device, The purpose of this research is to develop a system that measures the position of a teacher and trajectory recording of the teacher from the head of the teacher as he or she moves upright in the classroom by using a laser range sensor. The laser range sensor used for measurement is a sensor that can perform precise distance measurement using the reflection of laser light. It has become a common sensor, as used in iPhones and autonomous robots. This sensor is installed in the classroom and the background difference is calculated from the measured data of the background and the teacher. Extracts a set of points that are to be used as the teacher from the background differences, and records the two-dimensional coordinates of the teacher from these points. The trajectory of the teacher moving through the classroom shows based on the recorded coordinates of the teacher. The results of the experiment showed that there was a large amount of noise, and in some cases the trajectory was outside of the classroom, and in other cases, the coordinates output were very different even though they were at the same position.

Author Keywords: Check Individually by Making Our Rounds in the Classroom

articleTitle: Study on Optimization Method of Cam Grinding Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Cam and camshaft are one of the most common and key parts in mechanical equipment. In the process of cam operation, the rotation of the cam pushes the air valve stem to move in accordance with the law, so the accuracy of cam contour curve determines the performance of mechanical equipment. For example, the camshaft in automobile engine, its product quality directly affects the dynamic performance of engine. It has great practical significance to improve the machining accuracy of mechanical equipment, especially for the key parts. In order to improve the accuracy of cam grinding, many scholars have done a tremendous amount of research on compensation control [1], [2], but there is little research on the design of speed controller from the contour angle error. In order to improving the precision of cam contour machining, the emphasis of this paper is to design a speed optimization controller which considers the cam contour erroras a efficient control.The cam manufacturing process based on CNC grinding wheel is usually completed by the linkage of the rotating axis (C axis) and the advancing and withdrawing axis (X axis) of the grinding wheel. Typically, the input data of the system is the lift meter which describes the cam contour curve, but the lift meter is not directly input the data of the two-axis servo system, so it is necessary to process the lift meter data [3]. In this paper, a contour curve generation model is developed by the inversion method to generate cam contour curve. Then, modeling the input sequence values of the system for the input sequence value of the cam grinding platform. Finally, a contour error model is developed for error analysis to improve the preparation accuracy.In cam machining, there are many factors affecting cam precision, the biggest one is the cam rotation angle and grinding wheel feed speed [4]. Constant angular velocity and constant linear velocity grinding are often used in the existing machining methods, but when the precision of machining parts is high, constant angular velocity grinding cannot meet the requirements. In the cam grinding, servo system hysteresis leads to the tracking errors in the C axis and X axis,which in turn synthesizes the contour error [5]. Therefore, it is very necessary to adjust the speed in the grinding process. The results of theoretical derivation and constant angular velocity grinding simulation show that the big grinding speed leads to big cam contour error and the small grinding speed leads to small cam contour error. According to the final value theorem, when the position loop gain keeps the system stable, the grinding speed V is proportional to the tracking error E. Following this principle, the fuzzy control method is utilized to adjust the grinding speed, on the basis of constant angular speed grinding, the grinding speed is re-planned. The error of parts can be reduced by increasing the grinding time in the area with large error. But blindly increase grinding time, will affect the efficiency of processing. Therefore, in reducing the error of parts, but also to take into account the overall grinding time. Therefore, according to the error, the main task of the algorithm is to increase the grinding time in the area with large error and decrease the grinding time in the area with small error. This needs to carry the effective control on the grinding speed. The formulation of the control rules consiste of the following three aspects. Firstly, the grinding speed can be reduced in the area with large contour error, that means the grinding time can be increased in this area, while the grinding speed can be increased in the area with small contour error. Secondly, the grinding speed is reduced in the area where the variation rate of contour error is large, that is the grinding time is increased in this area, and the grinding speed is reduced in the area where the variation rate of contour error is small. Thirdly, setting a threshold for the contour error, which is the maximum contour error specified by the control algorithm, when the absolute value of the contour error exceeds the set threshold. When the absolute value of the contour error is less than the set threshold value, the controller does not work, and the original grinding speed remains unchanged. Since there is no feedback value of the contour error at the beginning of the system, the fuzzy controller can not work on the system, the controller controls the second grinding cycle. After the controller adjusts the grinding speed, when the absolute value of the contour error is less than the threshold value, the controller stops working to abtain the final results of the whole grinding process.In the grinding system, the given values of the cam rotating shaft and the grinding wheel feed shaft correspond to the grinding time of the adjacent grinding points respectively. Because of the change of grinding time between grinding points, the grinding process is no longer constant angular velocity grinding. In order to realize the change of grinding speed, a variable time-length Zero-order hold is proposed on the basis of Zero-order hold. The output characteristic curve of variable Zero-order hold is shown in Fig. 1. The sampling time T of the Zero-order hold is a constant value. If the value of the sampling time T is changed during the control process, the variable time Zero-order hold can be obtained. The grinding speed can be changed by the action of time-varying Zero-order hold. The function of time-varying Zero-order hold is realized by cubic spline interpolation.Taking the MK8312C CNC cam grinding machine tool as the research object. The CNC incorporates a three-closed-loop control system, where a position loop is added to the traditional double-closed-loop control system. The position signal output from the system is fed back to the input, which improves the response speed of the two axes and the tracking precision of the system. Simulink is used to build the two-axis simulation system of cam grinding, and MATLAB is used to design the fuzzy controller, and the fuzzy rules are input into the controller. The table of fuzzy rules is shown in Table 1, as shown in Fig. 2, the input of the fuzzy controller is the contour error and the contour error change rate, and the output is the time interval of the adjacent grinding points after fuzzy control The constant angular speed grinding and the speed optimization simulation grinding of fuzzy control are carried out on the cam. The simulation results are shown in Fig. 3. The blue curve is the contour error curve of constant angular velocity grinding, and the red curve is the contour error curve after the first optimization of fuzzy control algorithm. The two curves have roughly the same trend. The optimized grinding period T=3.631 s, the maximum absolute value of contour error is 1.023364938 mm, and the average absolute value of contour error is 0.220922157 mm. Compared with the constant angular speed grinding, the grinding time is increased by 0.86% , the maximum value of contour error is reduced by 22.83% , and the average value of contour error is reduced by 17.93%. The results of simulation show that compared with constant angular velocity grinding this method not only ensures the machining efficiency, but also greatly reduces the maximum and the average value of the absolute value of cam contour error.

articleTitle: A Novel Switched-Inductor merged SEPIC-Cuk Converter with Enhanced Voltage Gain
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel high voltage gain DC-DC converter that operates without a transformer, relying on switched-inductor. The proposed bi-directional converter achieves a notable increase in voltage gain and exhibits enhanced versatility by supporting both buck and boost execution in both power flow directions. This is achieved while minimizing stress on the components. The converter maintains a continuous input current and offers a bipolar output, making it well-suited for interfacing sustainable energy sources (SES) with a Bipolar DC microgrid (BPDCMG). Moreover, owing to its bidirectional feature, the proposed converter is adept at interfacing energy storage components (ESC) like batteries or ultracapacitors with the NPC inverter in an EV drive train. The paper illustrates the operating principles and steady-state analysis of the proposed converter. It further explores dynamic modelling and controller design to ensure regulation of source current and load voltage. Simulation results are presented to substantiate the efficacy of the introduced converter.

articleTitle: Adaptive-Control of Controlled Floating Space Robots Based on Fully-Actuated System Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: As human exploration of extraterrestrial space deepens, traditional space robots face challenges in effectively completing missions due to a growing demand for on-orbit service and several realistic factors. Consequently, controlled floating space robot has become a more significant research subject. However, its complex dynamic characteristics make current control techniques difficult to directly apply for adaptive-control. Consider that the contraction theory has promising performance in complex system control, this paper addresses the complex dynamic model of controlled floating space robots and combines the theory of parameter system reconstruction in fully-actuated systems with contraction theory to design efficient adaptive controller, in order to mitigate the impact of space perturbations and input constraints. This paper provides new perspectives for adaptive-control in the domain of space robotics.

articleTitle: Adaptive decentralized fault-tolerant control of nonlinear large-scale systems with actuator faults and unknown Strong Interconnections
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this article, a decentralized adaptive fault-tolerant control(FTC) scheme is proposed for a class of large-scale nonlinear systems with unknown time-varying parameters, actuator faults and unknown strong interconnections. Firstaccording to the fundamental traits of Gaussian function for the interconnection terms, the interference of interconnection terms to the system is eliminated effectively. Second, By employing command filter technique and adaptive neural control, the "singular" and "explosion of complex" problems in the backstepping procedure are circumvented. It is shown that all the closed-loop signals are bounded and the tracking errors converge to arbitrarily small residual sets. Finally, the effectiveness of decentralized adaptive fault-tolerant control scheme is demonstrated by simulation results.

articleTitle: Models and Methods for Steady-State Analysis of Radial Multi-Energy Grids and Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The interconnection between different energy networks leads to interdependencies that require suitable models and methods for their analysis. This paper presents appropriate models and methods for integrated and steady-state analysis of radial multi-energy grids and microgrids. The mathematical models of energy grids, including electrical, natural gas, and thermal grids, are formulated, solved jointly and validated by applying them to a case study. Prior to the resolution stage of this case study, three iterative methods for the numerical resolution of the radial multi-energy grid model are discussed with their advantages and disadvantages. It is concluded that the Newton-Raphson method with numerical Jacobian matrix reduces researcher workload, but at the cost of additional iterations for convergence, which is perfectly acceptable considering that the analytical calculation of the Jacobian matrix by the researcher and its subsequent programming are avoided.

articleTitle: Path Planning Strategy of Inchworm-like Robots Based on RAG-RRT* Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a random adaptive growth RRT* (RAG-RRT*) algorithm for pipe avoidance by inchworm-like robots. Firstly, we introduce the Manhattan Distance to measure the robot joint distance in the multidimensional space and add the goal bias to improve the goal-directed exploration performance of the algorithm. Then, the node growth weights are calculated by the distance between the new node and the target point, and the joint motion trajectories are optimized by adaptively changing the growth method. At the same time, random adaptive growth is used to maintain the spatial searchability of the algorithm. Finally, the total number of nodes and path quality were compared between different algorithms by building a robot and obstacle model in the MATLAB platform, and it was verified that the RAG-RRT* algorithm effectively improved the search efficiency, reduced the number of iterations, and optimized the path quality and length.

articleTitle: Two-step acceleration/deceleration for vibration-damped transfer of a 1DOF overhead traveling crane under open/closed-loop finite-time settling control using solutions of a two-point boundary value problem with half-odd-integer trigonometric functions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This study proposes a finite-time settling function that satisfies a two-point boundary value problem. The function consists of trigonometric functions with a period equal to half-odd integer multiples of the operation time. This function is applied to both open-loop and closed-loop finite-time settling controls. A computational simulation of vibration-damped transfer for an overhead crane was conducted. Without external disturbances, two-step vibration-damping acceleration/deceleration operations were performed. In the open-loop finite-time settling control, residual vibration persisted when the non-linearity of the pendulum was not neglected. On the other hand, residual vibrations were effectively suppressed in the closed-loop finite-time settling control, even during high-speed transfer with a large swing-up angle.

articleTitle: Analysis of Influencing Factors of Parallel Current Sharing of High Power Module
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The multi-chip power module serves as the core component of high-power Solid State Power Controller (SSPC). However, discrepancies in the intrinsic parameters of parallel-connected chips and the layout structure of the module result in uneven current distribution among parallel chips, significantly compromising the reliability of SSPC. This paper focuses on a developed 270V/200A power module and establishes an equivalent circuit model considering the parasitic parameters of the module’s actual structure. Firstly, simulations were conducted to observe the current sharing among parallel power Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistors (MOSFETs) under various operating modes. Secondly, a typical equivalent circuit model of a power module with three parallel branches was established. By altering the parasitic parameters of the MOSFET itself and the module’s layout structure, an analysis was carried out to investigate the impact of the imbalance in internal parasitic parameters on the module’s parallel current-sharing capability. Simulation results indicate that the steady-state current sharing capability of the power module is significantly influenced by stray resistances and MOSFET’s on-state resistances. Transient current sharing capability, on the other hand, is greatly affected by MOSFET’s threshold voltage, transconductance, gate drive resistance, and the parasitic inductance of the power circuit’s source busbar. Parasitic inductances of the gate drive circuit and drain copper busbar have minimal impact on transient current balance.

articleTitle: Exact Electrical Equivalent Circuit Model for Analysis of Permanent Magnet Direct Current (PMDC) Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this study, the electromechanical equations of the permanent magnet direct current (PMDC) motor are examined and a fully electrical equivalent circuit model is proposed. Generally, for DC motor models, only the electrical circuit model of the armature circuit is given, and the equations of the mechanical system are used. In this study, an electrically equivalent circuit model with the same equation structure as the mechanical system is proposed. Thus, both the armature circuit and the mechanical part of a PMDC motor are expressed with electrical circuit elements and parameters. Since the proposed model is a completely electrical circuit, mechanical quantities can be analyzed with circuit simulation programs. With the analyses, the performance of the permanent magnet DC motor model was examined and the system dynamics responses were found to be compatible.

articleTitle: Generalized high-speed vibration-damping transfer cam curve with arbitrary rise time in point symmetry consisting of half-odd-integer trigonometric functions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In the present investigation, we have proposed universal formulas for point symmetrical high-speed vibration-damping transport cams for a 1DOF undamped follower vibrator in an arbitral rise time. These formulas, composed of half-odd integer trigonometric functions, are deduced as solutions to a two-point boundary value problem. We evaluated the behavior of non-dwell and two-dwell cam profiles with low wavenumbers through simulations. Also, we show infinite linear sums of these formulas can express smooth and practical cam profiles comprising elementary and non-elementary functions. These formulations facilitate various expressions of the cam function, thereby broadening its potential.
