articleTitle: An MPC-Based Oscillation Suppression Strategy for IBRs connected to weak grids through LCL filters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper presents a model predictive control (MPC) based oscillation suppression strategy for LCL-type grid-connected inverters in weak grids. A hybrid cost function is developed to efficiently implement virtual damping and seamless transfer schemes. The method elaborates on different control modes for normal and under-transition operations. The LCL filter's voltage across the grid side inductor is utilised to derive the reference current to minimise transient oscillation and limit current spikes. The developed scheme will switch the MPC's reference current and cost function to manage different oscillations for inverter-based interconnections. Simulation results will prove the feasibility of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: A Subspace-aided Fault Diagnosis Approach for Electrical Drive Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: For the safe operation of electrical drive systems, a data-driven fault diagnosis approach is proposed by subspace-aided signal reconstruction in this paper. Specifically, based on the subspace identification method (SIM), the frequency estimation of the signal is reformulated into the eigenvalue identification, which can be directly extracted from the time-domain signal. The subspace frequency estimation approach can avoid the problem of spectrum leakage. Under the known frequency estimation, the amplitude and phase estimation are adopted by the least squares (LS) method. The signal is reconstructed for fault detection by estimating frequency, phase, and amplitude. The fault detection scheme is designed to be helpful for the implementation of fault diagnosis in the periodic signal. Eventually, the effectiveness of the proposed approach is verified.

articleTitle: Grid Resilience Enhancement through TPTL NPC Inverter-Based Shunt Active Power Filters with Dual Fundamental Component Extraction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The extensive use of nonlinear loads in power distribution systems has led to significant concerns about power quality. Therefore, this article emphasizes the generation of accurate sinusoidal reference currents to effectively reduce harmonics and maintain sinusoidal current, even under non-ideal grid voltage conditions. Furthermore, a time domain-based algorithm for generating reference currents to minimize dc-link voltage deviation in the TPTL NPC-based SAPF. The suggested algorithm concurrently extracts the necessary fundamental current and voltage components in order to generate reference current and synchronization phases. Consequently, this algorithm can produce reference currents that ensure the SAPF operates in phase with the system, without relying on PLL. The efficacy of the presented algorithm has been comprehensively examined and assessed using MATLAB-Simulink. The suggested control scheme has also been validated experimentally, with results indicating satisfactory overall system performance even when subjected to changing load scenarios.

articleTitle: Cyber Attack-Aware Security Hardening of Time Synchronization Technologies in WAMPAC Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Synchrophasor-based wide-area monitoring, protection, and control (WAMPAC) applications have been recently prevalent in modern power systems to counteract system-wide operational concerns. However, the functionality of the WAMPAC application is significantly contingent on the precision and integrity of time-synchronization mechanisms which are vulnerable to time-synchronization attacks (TSAs). To counter TSAs targeting WAMPAC applications, this paper proposes a preventive countermeasure by attack-aware security hardening of time synchronization technologies (TSTs) in substations houses critical phasor measurement units (PMUs). The attack-aware security hardening problem is formulated as a bi-level operator-attack model. This model aims to minimize post-TSA error of the PMU-based AC state estimation (ACSE), a critical module for a majority of WAMPAC applications, by optimal allocating a set of security hardening respecting the limited operator budget. The operator layer obtains security hardening strategy and under-TSA system states while the attacker layer optimizes attack vector and manipulated phasor measurements. Using the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) approach, the developed model is recast to a single-level quadratic mixed-integer linear problem tackle-able using mathematical solvers. The numerical results on the IEEE 39-Bus test system demonstrate that the proposed preventive countermeasure can significantly reduce the attacker’s ability to maliciously impact ACSE module.

articleTitle: Effect of Eccentric Tooth Tip Arc on Cogging Torque of PM Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper proposes an eccentric tooth tip arc on a stator for a reduction in the cogging torque of permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSM). The proposed technique is applicable for both inner rotor and outer rotor PM machines. The variation in the stator tooth geometry and a corresponding change in the tooth tip arc of the eccentric tooth is derived mathematically. Two different PM synchronous motors, i.e. 12-slot/10-pole inner rotor and 12-slot/14-pole outer rotor PMSM are taken for this study to analyze the effect of the proposed method. A detailed finite element analysis (FEA) is performed on both the machines, and their cogging torque is analyzed. It is found that the cogging torque reduces with an increase in the eccentricity of the stator tooth tip arc.

articleTitle: Fault-Tolerant Electric Vehicle Drivetrain with Reconfigurable Battery and Multiphase Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper describes a reconfigurable battery design to drive a multiphase machine in an electric vehicle and a control of the battery balance as well as the motor. On the other hand, the dynamically reconfigurable battery uses its inherent topological potential to directly connect to the grid and charge the batteries. All the modules can actually integrate and play the role of a converter which can charge the batteries with a unity power factor and minimum additional components. The results demonstrate various operating modes including charging of the battery as well as the operation of the motor under multiple failures in modules. As expected, the speed range can be maintained, and the active modules compensate the whole system for the current loss of the inactive modules, confirming high system tolerance to module failure in the system.

articleTitle: CSE-YOLOv5: A Lightweight Attention Guided YOLOv5 Network based on EIoU Loss
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Ship detection using synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images poses several challenges, primarily due to the small size and low resolution of ships in these images resulting from long observation distances. To solve this problem, we optimize the fifth generation version of you only look once through channel attention, spatial attention and efficient intersection over union (CSE-YOLOv5). The CSE-YOLOv5 improves the detection accuracy of small targets with almost no sacrifice of the real-time performance of the algorithm. Specifically, we design network of YOLOv5 based on convolutional block attention module (CBAM). In order to improve the detection accuracy and training efficiency, a new loss function constraint detection bounding box is employed, so that the detector can learn the position of the ship target more effectively. Experimental results on multiple public SAR datasets show that the average precision (AP) of CSE-YOLOv5 can reach 96% in SAR ship detection dataset (SSDD) and 69.1% in large-scale SAR ship detection dataset dataset (LS-SSDD), which is an increase of 2.6% and 3.8% respectively over the previous improvement. Compare with the current mainstream object detection algorithms, the model has better object performance.

articleTitle: Toolset Development for Modelling Sympathetic Phenomenon and its Detection by a Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: One of the most important elements of any AC power supply system is the transformer. Each stakeholder, such as Distribution Network Operators (DNOs), Transmission System Operators (TSOs), and other generators, is paying close attention to investigating possible negative impacts that could disrupt the normal distribution of electricity. One of them is short-term transient processes that occur in the network when the transformer core is turned on. These transients can cause significant distortion on the power line, which in turn can cause nuisance tripping of protection devices. For a small and isolated electrical system, this is not usually considered a major problem. However, as the electrical grid grows, this becomes more important. This is a problem that machine learning can help with. However, the problem is that there is currently no significant data on the transformer excitation phenomenon.This article gives a brief explanation of transformer excitation phenomena in an introductory section. With this information in mind, we developed a SIMULINK model and a MATLAB script to describe and automatically run a new experiment design and generate data. Finally, we use the generated data as a training dataset to fit it into a supervised convolutional neural network. The final data set that we created and used for the purposes of this work, as well as the SIMULINK model and the MATLAB script for automatically generating the experiment design, are in the public domain.

articleTitle: Sequential Predictive Torque Control of a Six-Phase Induction Machine fed by a Multi-Modular Direct Matrix Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Multiphase induction machines, known for their higher torque density, improved fault tolerance, and reduced harmonic losses, are well-suited for high-power applications. This paper presents a sequential model predictive torque control approach for a multi-modular direct matrix converter-driven six-phase induction machine. The direct matrix converter offers advantages such as direct AC-AC conversion, unity power factor operation, and low harmonic distortion. Simulation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme in achieving accurate reference tracking for torque, flux, and stator currents. This research advances MPC-based control strategies for DMC applications in multiphase machines.

articleTitle: Distributed Optimal Collaborative Control for Linear Multi-Agent Systems under Switching Topology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This article addresses the distributed optimal coordination control (DOC) problem of linear multi-agent systems (MAS) under switching communication topology. Firstly, the distributed optimization goal is minimize team objective function in a multi-agent system, where each local objective function has one node knows, and each multi-agent only utilizes both of local interaction information and the gradient of owns local objective function. Secondly, a new DOC control algorithm is proposed, it shows that asymptotic convergence can be verified by analyzing the stability of consensus errors. Finally, simulation results are provided.

articleTitle: Mathematical model and control of a three-level boost converter used as electronic interface for fuel cell vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Several topologies of dc-dc converters have been developed seeking a high voltage gain, high capability to power processing and high efficiency. The complete modeling of these devices allows the proper choice of components, as well as the design of controllers. This paper presents an average and small-signal modeling of the three-level boost converter (TLBC) characterized by reduced stress on switches, low electromagnetic interference and low voltage and current ripple. The static voltage gain of the converter is calculated based on the developed model and the influence of all parasitic resistances is evaluated, resulting in a graphical analysis and equations that allow the design of the components. Theoretical analysis and the mathematical results obtained are validated through simulations. A cascade control for terminal voltage is developed using PI controllers designed by the frequency response and root locus diagram obtained by the modeling. The results verify that the output voltage is maintained at the reference value in a vehicular application.

articleTitle: A cooperative positioning algorithm based on adaptive selection and factor graph
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The cooperative positioning technology based on Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) is one of the most rapidly developing underwater positioning technologies in recent years, it can complete complex underwater tasks that are difficult for a single AUV to complete, and has broad development prospects. Due to the complex underwater environment, fuzzy time-varying noise may be generated, which may also lead to changes in the system structure, the number of leader AUVs is numerous and the quality is complex. These factors can lead to a decrease in the accuracy and efficiency of traditional algorithms. To address these issues, we propose a cooperative positioning algorithm based on dynamic structure-based adaptive selection and Factor Graph (DS-AOSFG). Systems with dynamic topology can effectively cope with structural changes. In response to fuzzy time-varying noise, we introduce an adaptive filter module. In response to the problem of many leader AUVs and mixed quality, we introduce a node optimization selection module and improve the traditional algorithm through the factor graph algorithm. The final evaluation indicates that our DS-AOSFG method outperforms other algorithms in terms of positioning accuracy and speed.

articleTitle: A Bifacial PV/Battery Three Port Hybrid System for Stand-alone Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Bifacial PV technology has brought about a significant transformation in the renewable energy sector, propelling photovoltaic systems to new heights. These systems are meticulously designed to boost performance and optimize power generation. In stark contrast to traditional PV modules, bifacial modules exhibit a distinctive capability to yield higher power outputs. However, the power output of PV systems is influenced by daily fluctuations in temperature and irradiance levels. Consequently, it is of paramount importance to maximize the efficiency of PV modules and extract the utmost available power. In the context of standalone bifacial PV applications, the existing literature lacks a proper technique for harnessing the maximum power potential. This paper addresses this gap by introducing a modified algorithm designed to estimate the maximum power output from bifacial PV systems. The same algorithm is then put to the test in a proposed bifacial PV/Battery triport hybrid system. Here, the battery serves as an energy storage component, enabling the regulation of the DC link voltage at a consistent level.

articleTitle: Towards web-applications for domain-specific languages and development tools
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The modern trend towards web-based technologies in different domains calls for innovative tooling frameworks that are both adaptive and robust. This paper introduces a novel architecture for web-based development tools, employing a thin-client approach and scalable micro-service architecture, which holds significance in the era of web technologies. Central to this framework is a reactive document analysis algorithm, which is based on the declarative description of formal domain concepts and analysis rules. Several domain-specific languages have been drafted for domains such as industrial automation systems, based on IEC 61499, and biological knowledge structuring, to evaluate the proposed architecture. The results indicate the viability of integrating such an approach in future web-based development environments, thereby enhancing the ease and efficiency of conducting code analysis and editing tasks. Moreover, the architecture lays a foundation for the evolution of development tools aligned with modern web technologies.

articleTitle: Predicting Remaining Discharge Time for Lithium-ion Batteries based on Differential Model Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper presents a method for estimating Remaining Dischargeable Time (RDT) with enhanced prognostic capabilities. The method introduces an innovative prognostic strategy to accurately predict RDT, utilizing the Differential Model Decomposition (DMD) method as the basis for its mathematical framework. The effectiveness of the proposed RDT prognostic method, equipped with built-in prognostic capabilities, is demonstrated through real battery degradation experiments. Finally, the performance of the RDT prognostic method is comprehensively assessed using various online prognostic evaluation metrics. The results indicate that the DMD approach improves the consistency of discharge patterns during long-term degradation.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of Controllable Pitch Propeller as Few-Shot Classification with Mechanism Simulation Data Augmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The Controllable pitch propeller(CPP) can control the thrust direction and power through the adjustment of blade pitch using a hydraulic system, significantly improving the maneuverability of the vessel. Given the harsh working environment of the on-ship CPP hydraulic system, it is prone to failure and affects pitch control performance. To address the challenges of limited real-world fault condition data, we utilize a few-shot learning approach and enhance the model’s sensitivity to target data distribution by introducing a simulation data augmentation phase during training. A mechanical model of the CPP hydraulic system is developed, and monitoring data under fault conditions of key components is simulated. After training with open-source time-series classification tasks, the augmentation phase is used to obtain prior knowledge of the equipment, and the model is eventually adapted to the recorded data task. The recorded data is derived from an experimental setup comprising the primary components of the CPP, and it is collected from multiple sensors under both normal and fault conditions. The target fault diagnosis task is treated as a time-series classification problem, and a network architecture based on ResNet with Triplet loss is employed.

articleTitle: Efficient coalitional model predictive control with Pareto optimal system partitioning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper proposes an efficient coalitional model predictive control algorithm with Pareto optimal system partitioning for coupled nonlinear systems. We consider a coupled nonlinear multi-agent system controlled by a set of local agents, which can be dynamically merged into coalitions for centralized control as certain similar characteristics or specific requirements arise. A modified continuation/generalized minimal residual (C/GMRES) algorithm is developed for the high- dimensional coalition dynamics that may arise in this process. Compared with the standard C/GMRES, the modified C/GMRES has been extended in the coalitional framework and a modified barrier function is integrated into the cost function to handle inequality constraints. In addition, to balance the conflict between communication cost and performance cost, a non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm is employed to search Pareto optimal system partitioning. Finally, the proposed algorithm is illustrated through a simulation example.

articleTitle: Cascaded Low-Pass and Band-Pass Filtering with Frequency Adaptation for Multifunctional Control of Grid Tied Inverter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper presents cascaded low-pass (LP) and band-pass (BP) filtering based multifunctional control of inverter interfacing distributed energy resource (DER) with the grid. Multifunctional control of grid tied inverter results in (a) control of active power being supplied by distributed energy resource to the grid, and (b) shunt active filtering through harmonic current mitigation and reactive power compensation. Cascaded LP-BP filtering extracts the fundamental active component of load current (FACL) for shunt active filtering. Without frequency adaptation, the cascaded LP-BP filtering would result in erroneous FACL extraction. To overcome this, the cascaded LP-BP filtering is employed in two stages. In the first stage, cascaded LP-BP filtering processes the grid voltages considering nominal grid frequency. Based on the output of this stage, the actual grid frequency is estimated. Second stage involves processing of load currents by the cascaded LP-BP filter method, using the estimated frequency, for determining the FACL. The incorporation of frequency adaption in cascaded LP-BP filtering results in improved accuracy for FACL estimation.

articleTitle: ENEST - Efficient Interrupt Nesting for RISC-V based CPUs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Embedded systems are typically driven by external and internal events, implemented by means of (static priority) interrupts. Response time can be improved by allowing for interrupt nesting, i.e., allowing for a higher priority interrupt to preempt the execution of a currently running interrupt handler. In this paper we study interrupt nesting for the RISC-V architecture and propose ENEST: a stacking approach with predictable overhead, minimizing both blocking and interference. Claims of the proposed mechanism are validated on the modern ESP32-C3 single core MCU. Our experimental results quantify blocking and interference, allowing further static scheduling analysis of ENEST based applications.

articleTitle: ADRC-based Event Triggering Control for Switched Nonlinear Systems with Actuator Faults
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this paper, an improved active disturbance rejection control scheme is proposed for a class of switched nonlinear systems with actuator faults by means of event triggering mechanism. To solve the problem of unknown states and unknown global disturbances in complex systems, an extended state observer is constructed to compensate the global disturbances in switched systems in real time. Then, an improved tracking differentiator is proposed, which can not only achieve the excellent tracking performance of the input signal by adjusting the parameters of the tracking differentiator, and the differential explosion problem under backstepping technique can be solved. Moreover, an event triggering algorithm is proposed to compensate the actuator faults of the system under the condition of saving communication resources. The proposed control method can ensure that all signals in the closed-loop system are semi-global ultimately uniformly bounded, and that the output signals track the reference signals well. Finally, simulation results of the classical RLC switching circuit show the effectiveness of the above-mentioned control research.

articleTitle: An Online Trajectory Planning Approach for Quadrotor Suspension Transportation Systems: Anti-swing and Obstacle Avoidance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper proposes an autonomous obstacle avoidance trajectory planning method of quadrotor-based flight suspension systems for anti-swing payload transportation. This paper analyzes the dynamics of the quadrotor-based flight suspension systems based on the Euler-Lagrange equation. B spline curves are designed to generate initial trajectories for the quadrotor, which can avoid known obstacles. Then, an angular coupling anti-swing term is designed and superimposed to the initial trajectory, so as to suppress payload swing during obstacle avoidance. A series of simulation results verify that the proposed method achieves satisfactory performance in obstacle avoidance and payload swing suppression from the trajectory planning level.

articleTitle: A real-time load positioning and recognition system integrating image segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Real-time positioning and recognition of loads lifted by tower cranes is essential for achieving intelligent tower crane operations in building construction process. Currently, the real-time collection system for load features employs a laser scanning technique, resulting in a large volume of data. It imposes high performance requirements on computing terminals, making it difficult to apply at a large scale in practical construction projects. Also, existing load positioning methods extract load features from the entire environmental dataset under complex construction site environments. It leads to difficulties in feature extraction due to the inclusion of redundant information. Furthermore, existing deep learning-based load recognition models are time-consuming to train. In this paper, a real-time load positioning and recognition system integrating image segmentation is proposed. Firstly, lifted loads of tower crane in construction sites is captured using a spherical network camera, and is transmitted to a computing terminal via the RTSP protocol in real-time. Secondly, the YOLOv5s algorithm is employed to eliminate environmental interference in tower crane surroundings, enabling the load positioning and segmentation based on the hook's location. Furthermore, the MobileNetV2 algorithm is utilized for load recognition to reduce computational cost. Lastly, a remote visual prototype system for load targets is designed and developed, providing real-time remote display and automatic recognition of tower crane loads. The proposed system has demonstrated excellent performance when tested on an engineering site dataset, focusing on tower crane usage in building construction for material handling.

articleTitle: Design of Common-Mode Transformer for Damping of High-Frequency Leakage Current in PAM Inverter-Fed Three Phase Brushless dc Motor Drive System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In Brushless dc (BLdc) motors, the commutation effect inherent to Pulse-Amplitude Modulation (PAM) can generate high-frequency leakage currents. To address this issue such as common-mode (CM) chokes are commonly employed. CM chokes can restrict the peak value of CM current within the limit dictated by application-specific standards. However, CM choke tends to be bulky and requires space, reducing power density. In contrast, common-mode transformers (CMTs) have emerged as an alternative solution for dampening high-frequency leakage currents while occupying less volume. Nevertheless, directly applying CMT designs from conventional induction motors to BLdc drives may result in oversized CMTs. This discrepancy arises because BLdc motors operate differently, affecting the nature of high-frequency leakage current generation. This paper presents a simple approach to CMT design specific to BLdc motors. A comparative analysis of the volume occupied by the custom-designed CMT in contrast to traditional CM chokes is presented. To substantiate the claims and assess the practicality of the CMT design, a 310 V, 1.5 kW silicon carbide (SiC)-fed three-phase BLdc drive is used.

articleTitle: Considerations of Extremum-Seeking Control based on the Sinusoidal Perturbation Applied to the MPPT Converter with PWM Modulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This article analyzes the extremum-seeking control based on sinusoidal perturbation applied to a maximum power point tracking (MPPT) converter with pulse width modulation (PWM). With the proposed algorithm it is possible for the MPPT converter to track the optimal set point, with a fast transient response, as evaluated through simulation results. Further details involving the proposed control algorithm and the MPPT converter performance were discussed throughout this paper as well.

articleTitle: Virtual sensing of aircraft extreme parameters based on parameter spatial-temporal correlation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Aircraft wing parameters are a key variable that reflects the status of the aircraft and evaluates the operational safety of the aircraft. Nevertheless, limited by the wing structure and harsh operating environment, it is difficult to measure wing parameters by deploying sensors and other methods. Simultaneously, the alterations in wing configuration and the intricate operating environment lead to dynamic variations in the coupling relationship between wing parameters, so it is difficult to use a single output model to fit the parameter changes. Therefore, this paper proposes a wing parameter uncertainty modeling method based on parameter spatial-temporal coupling. This paper establishes a mapping model that links measurable characteristics (such as airspeed, Aileron angle, etc.) with unmeasurable parameters (such as Aileron, etc.) in order to enable the measurement perception of these parameters. Furthermore, this paper employs Bayesian inference to assess the level of uncertainty in the model's output. Ultimately, this paper employs the airplane simulation data set to validate the suggested approach.

articleTitle: Seamless transition of inverters from islanding to grid-connected mode connected to weak grid
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The fundamental principle of integrating a voltage source within an electrical network to enhance voltage control and promote network stability remains a core tenet of electrical engineering. In scenarios characterized by weak grid conditions, where voltage fluctuations and instability are prevalent, a strategic solution involves the synergistic deployment of both Grid-Forming (GFM) and Grid-Following (GFL) inverters. This integrated approach is designed to address the inherent drawbacks associated with fragile grid infrastructures, ultimately improving the reliability and performance of the electrical network. This paper presents a comparative analysis when GFM inverters are integrated with GFL inverters in a microgrid (MG). The MG network is connected to the weak grid through a seamless transition from islanded to grid-connected mode. Through MATLAB/SIMULINK simulations, it highlights voltage and frequency stability challenges during transient conditions, providing valuable insights into weak grid connections.

articleTitle: Path Planning Scheme for AUV Based on Improved Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this paper, a path planning scheme for Model Predictive Control (MPC) of autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) is proposed based on conditional penalty function. Traditionally, MPC-based path planning schemes use the squared difference between the current and target positions as the cost function, and consider the size of the obstacle plus a minimum safety radius as constraints. However, such methods may lead to the AUV closely following the minimum safety radius, leaving insufficient time to react to unexpected situations. To address this issue, a soft constraint is introduced into the cost function using a conditional penalty function. This allows for a relative safer distance between the AUV and obstacles to be maintained in certain situations. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Automated Workstation for Lithium-ion Battery Cycling, Spectroscopy and Custom Profile for Cell Characterization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This study presents the design of an experimental setup for the automated cycling and spectroscopic analysis of lithium-ion cells to improve efficiency in generating data. This allows us to address challenges in estimating energy storage device’s health and autonomy. These challenges make it necessary to use charging and discharging with customized profiles and integrate exhaustive Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy analysis during these processes. This work proposes the interconnection of different equipment to carry out synchronized experiments. The results show the system’s ability to perform charge, discharge, and cell characterization tests in a temperature-controlled environment. This approach contributes significantly to the understanding and managing of lithium-ion cells in various applications, from transportation to renewable energy storage, by offering an automated and versatile tool for realist experimental data generation. The main contributions of this paper lie in developing a lithium-ion workstation that allows the complete design and execution of complex experiments.

articleTitle: Control Strategies Proposals in Grid-Connected Converters: Balancing Inverter Output Current Limitation and Power Injection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper offers a comprehensive analysis of interconnecting a converter to the electrical grid through an LCL filter, focusing on the control strategy and its alternative approaches. The control strategy includes an external power control mechanism, translating power into a constrained reference current. Additionally, an internal current controller utilizing state feedback is implemented. The study investigates multiple strategies to strike a balance between limiting the inverter output current and precisely injecting power into the grid. Different techniques are assessed, some prioritizing effective limitation of inverter output current but facing challenges in achieving the desired power injection. Conversely, alternative methods efficiently inject the desired power but encounter difficulties in guaranteeing a limited inverter output current. Moreover, this paper conducts simulations to compare the behavior of these strategies under uncertainties in electrical parameters and during weak grid scenarios. The simulations underscore the pivotal role of this mechanism in significantly enhancing the efficiency and reliability of the converter connected to the grid.

articleTitle: Analysis of the peak and RMS current ratios in a dual active bridge converter with triangular modulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this paper, new current management ratios (CMRs) useful for managing the conduction loss, current stress, and inductor or transformer saturation are developed for a triangular modulated dual active bridge (TriMDAB) converter. The CMRs include Peak-to-DC current (P2D), RMS-to-DC current (R2D), and Peak-to-RMS current (P2R) ratios. The P2D, R2D, and P2R are respectively useful for the minimisation of the peak current, RMS current, or both. The lower the ratios, the better the performance of the converter. Firstly, the inductor peak, inductor RMS and the output (DC link) currents formulae are derived analytically. These are used to obtain the formulae for the ratios and provided useful insight about the relationship among the converter variables. The formulae developed for the ratios are simpler to use by design engineers than the inductor peak and RMS current formulae. The theory was verified by comparing the calculated ratios with the PLECS<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> simulated values. The respective ratios for both cases perfectly matched. Besides the use of efficiency, the ratios further provided an alternative standard way of measuring the performance of DAB converters at different powers which engineers usually struggle with. The TriMDAB converter is usually operated in two cases: (1.) when input voltage is greater than the referred output voltage, or (2.) when the former is less than the latter. Our investigation recommends operation in the first case since there are reduced CMRs in the region.

articleTitle: Anomalous traffic detection algorithm for SDN
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: With the rapid development of the Internet, network security and related technologies have become a topic of public concern. A new network architecture—SDN, began to attract widespread attention. The SDN network architecture has the characteristics of centralized control and programmability, which can obtain the network topology and traffic information of the entire network. At the same time, the SDN network can manage the entire network at the control layer and take countermeasures at the control layer to respond to network attacks quickly. However, due to the open nature of SDN, SDN network is also more vulnerable to cyberattacks.To solve the problem of SDN network security, this paper proposes a machine learning algorithm of LightGBM combined with the CNN algorithm to realize network abnormal traffic detection and achieve a good classification effect. Firstly, the LightGBM is used to identify abnormal network traffic, and the model can process large data volumes efficiently, which makes the proposed method applied to the security assurance of large-scale SDN networks effectively. At the same time, the CNN algorithm is used to classify the identified network abnormal traffic. Using a 10% subset of the KDD CUP 99 dataset for experimental verification, this combined machine learning algorithm can effectively identify 22 types of abnormal traffic, effectively improving the recognition accuracy.

articleTitle: Two-Channel Event-Triggered Model Predictive Control for Optimal Operation of Office Buildings
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this paper, a novel two-channel event-triggered model predictive control (ET-MPC) is proposed to achieve the optimal operation of office buildings. The thermal Resistance-Capacitance (RC) network of the office building is established by the heat balance equation to reflect the indoor thermal environment. Two event-triggered mechanisms are introduced both on the sensor and controller sides based on two-channel ET-MPC, which can more effectively reduce energy consumption and communication resources while optimizing the system performance. The convergence analysis of the two-channel ET-MPC algorithm is given. Finally, the co-simulation experiment of MATLAB and EnergyPlus based on Ptolemy II shows that the proposed algorithm can save about 50% of the office building energy consumption.

articleTitle: A study of the optimal poses based calibration method for kinematic parameters of Stewart robot
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Due to the high stiffness and load capacity, the Stewart robot is widely used in the high-end manufacturing. However, the accuracy performance of Stewart robot is affected by various factors. This paper carries out a study on the accuracy improvement method of the Stewart robot. The proposed method is composed of the kinematic calibration and the tool transformation calibration methods. The optimal poses are selected by the IOOPS algorithm based on the observational index O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>. The optimal pose number is determined as 75. Several experiments have been done to evaluate the performance of the proposed method. The experimental results show that the average position error and average attitude error of the Stewart robot is reduced from (0.4937mm, 0.0346°) to (0.0067mm, 0.003°). The position and attitude accuracy performance is improved by 98.6% and 91.3% respectively. It can be seen that the proposed calibration method can efficiently improve the robot accuracy performance.

articleTitle: A New Design Technique for Pole-changing Induction Motors Considering Drive Cycle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Permanent magnet motors, which have a greater power density and better efficiency, are more commonly used in electric vehicles. However, when these motors are operated in a wide-speed range, their efficiency reduces. Consequently, it is necessary to seek alternatives. Multi-phase induction motors offer greater torque densities and fault tolerance compared to conventional induction motor drives. These motors are also capable of pole reconfiguration, enabling them to operate over a greater spectrum of torque and speed. This serves to extract more power during regeneration, thereby reducing the total energy consumption over the entire drive cycle. This study examines the suitable pole-pair combinations for a given torque-speed requirement in order to reduce the overall energy consumption of the system over a drive-cycle. ANSYS MAXWELL 2D is used for FEM analysis of designed machines. Using MATLAB/Simulink, mathematical models of the pole-changing induction motor and vehicle have been created for investigation. Simulation results of MAXWELL 2D and MATLAB/Simulink has been found to be effective in selecting the right pole combination.

articleTitle: Dynamic Behavior Modeling of Analog Circuits Based on Deep Operator Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Analog circuits are widely used in audio amplification, computing, power amplification, radio communication, etc. It is crucial to design a reliable circuit health monitoring system. Neural networks (NNs) are general-purpose approximators of continuous functions, however, a little-known but powerful finding is that a neural network with a single hidden layer can accurately approximate any nonlinear continuous operator. The general approximation theorem for operators extends point-topoint mapping to function-to-function mapping, forming the deep operator network (DeepONet). The zero-state response of an analog electrical circuit is equivalent to a convolution operator. This paper aims to use DeepONet to model the physical dynamic behavior of the second-order band-pass filter analog circuit, complete the function mapping from the input end (excitation) to the output end (zero-state response) of the circuit, and then learn the entire filtering function of the circuit. After the network model is trained, we can obtain the output function value of any time point of the circuit for any input of the circuit, to achieve real-time monitoring of the circuit, which is of great significance for improving the system reliability.

articleTitle: Control Synthesis of a Buck-Derived Active Energy Storage System in PV Microinverter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) microinverters traditionally implement passive electrolytic capacitor (EC) banks as an energy storage medium in the DC link for mitigating the double-line frequency power ripple arising from mismatched DC and AC port power. Such an energy storage medium reduces the magnitude of the resultant DC link voltage ripple. An EC bank solution, however, is severely detrimental to the realizable microinverter power density and reliability. To address this issue, this paper proposes an alternative solution for DC link energy storage in the form of a buck-derived pulsating power buffer (PPB) circuit which enables improvement both in power density and reliability of the microinverter system. Furthermore, this paper focuses on modeling the PPB power stage dynamics and thereby development of a cascaded control scheme featuring grid frequency tracking. The proposed methodology in this work is validated by simulation and hardware prototype for a PPB installed a the front-end of a single-stage PV microinverter system rated for 40VDC to 120VAC nominal voltage conversion at 400W rated load. It is found that the proposed PPB has 98.79% rated load efficiency which reduces the overall system efficiency by 0.57%, exhibits small steady-state error, and reacts rapidly to properly regulate reactive power over inverter load variation.

articleTitle: PIDPipe: A Pipeline for Digitizing P&ID with Unsupervised Symbol Localization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Digitizing Piping and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs) is challenging since the information is loosely structured in the document. Mostly supervised learning has been used by researchers to extract the information from P&IDs. However, having good quality labels, particularly, for localizing the symbols that require tight bounding boxes on the symbols, is difficult. In this research work, we propose a pipeline for digitizing P&IDs called PIDPipe with an unsupervised method for symbol localization. We analyze our method on a dataset of synthetic and real P&IDs. Our method achieved an accuracy of 71.3%, 72%, 52%, 74% and 81% for text detection, text recognition, symbol localization, and solid and broken line detection, respectively. This digitized information can be used towards the automated creation of Human Machine Interfaces and Digital Twins.

articleTitle: DeviceVeri-A Graphical Programming Based Test Script Generation Framework for Measurement Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Manufacturing and Process Industries use a complex and wide range of measurement devices to measure real-time process variables like temperature, pressure, and flow rate. Control systems use the measured process variables to manage various industrial operations like opening/closing a valve, raising alarms, etc. Inaccurate recording of process variables can lead to industrial failures or affect the production quality of manufactured goods. Verification of measurement devices thus becomes imperative to ensure maximum performance of industrial processes. Traditionally, subject matter experts and testers define the pseudo logic of a test case, which software developers further convert to executable test scripts to be run on devices. However, this manual generation of test scripts is cumbersome, time-consuming, lacks standardization, and depends mainly on the software developers’ competency. Automatic generation of test scripts thus becomes necessary for quick, reliable, and efficient testing of measurement devices.This paper presents a device verification framework called DeviceVeri, based on graphical programming to generate executable test scripts for verifying measurement devices. General and device-specific graphical blocks represent specific functionalities of device verification logic. Graphical blocks abstract technical details from users, making the test script generation process simple, less time-intensive, and user-friendly. The framework will be used by process engineers, testers and subject matter experts to generate test scripts and use them to verify measurement devices. In addition, the proposed framework minimizes the dependency on software developers to write test scripts manually, thus enhancing the testing process of measurement devices.

articleTitle: Study of high-current press-fit connectors for electrical performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Connectors for bringing high currents in and out of circuit boards are undergoing a significant evolution to meet the contemporary demand across various applications, including electric automotive, renewable energy, and automation. The development of high-current connectors has advanced considerably, moving away from traditional soldering methods to modern solderless press-fit connectors. This study subjects two high-current connector types, namely with solid press-fit and compliant press-fit pins, to a comprehensive evaluation based on both mechanical and electrical parameters. An experimental setup was meticulously prepared to measure the press-in force in relation to displacement. The choice of one connector over the other is determined mainly by application, but factors such as geometry, material and press-in forces can be equally important. Given the growing requirements for higher current and power capacities even in everyday applications, the impartial performance evaluation of these connectors becomes imperative for a deeper understanding and their effective use in various domains.

articleTitle: Dynamic performance of BINSYM under load and speed variation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Electrified transportation is gaining popularity due to environmental concerns over IC engines. Researchers are recently looking for a brushless and permanent magnet (PM)-less solution for electric vehicle motors. Wound-field synchronous motor (WFSM) could be a suitable alternative to PM-based machines. Brushless Induction excited Synchronous Motor (BINSYM) is a WFSM where the exciter, an induction machine (IM), is embedded inside a synchronous machine (SM) frame. The SM and IM are wound for different numbers of poles to achieve magnetic decoupling. The purpose of IM is to control the field excitation of SM. The IM is controlled in plugging mode at a constant slip frequency over the entire speed range to minimize its reactive power demand. The maximum torque per ampere (MTPA) and rms current minimization algorithm are used to control the SM. Simulation of the BINSYM-based system has been carried out in MATLAB/Simulink to validate the control strategies.

articleTitle: A local data-based method to reduce the zone2 operation time of distance relay
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Conventional distance protection scheme initiates the trip command for zone-2 internal fault after some intentional delay. This delayed operation of the relay is the main cause of the major blackout that has occurred across the world. This issue can be resolved based on the status of the remote end circuit breaker using a communication channel between sending and receiving ends. However, communication assisted zone-2 acceleration schemes fails in case of communication failure, and the communication links are not available for all transmission networks. To solve these issues, a local data-based algorithm to reduce zone-2 operation time of distance relay is presented in this paper. The proposed scheme detects the opening of the remote end circuit breaker (CB) by calculating the fault location utilizing the local end voltage and current signal. The suggested method is not affected by change in fault resistance, load angle, and pre-fault system condition; also, it can easily differentiate between internal and external fault. The performance of the said algorithm is evaluated using MATLAB software package for different fault resistance, fault location, and pre-fault system condition. The simulation result reveals that the algorithm detects the operation of the remote CB, which can be used to reduce the zone-2 operation time of the distance relay.

articleTitle: Comparison of Various Modulation Techniques for Conventional, Quasi and Switched Inductor Z-Source Inverter Topologies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Pulse width modulation (PWM) inverters are essential elements in various applications requiring dc-ac conversion. In PWM inverters, the rms output voltage in the range of 0-100% of the applied dc-link voltage and an increase in the rms value beyond the dc-link voltage are not possible. Z-source inverters (ZSIs) incorporate an impedance network in the conventional power structure of PWM inverters. With this they are able to provide the rms output voltage higher than the dc-link voltage. The three main ZSI topologies that are widely reported are: (i) conventional ZSI, (ii) quasi-ZSI (q-ZSI), and (iii) switched inductor ZSI (SI-ZSI). Similarly, the three commonly employed modulation techniques reported for ZSIs are: (i) simple boost control (SBC), (ii) maximum boost control (MBC), and (iii) third harmonic maximum boost control (THBMC). This paper presents the simulation-based implementation of all the above-mentioned modulation techniques for conventional ZSI, quasi ZSI (q-ZSI) and switched inductor ZSI (SI-ZSI). Based on the simulation study, the paper presents a detailed comparison of the performance of ZSI topologies using different modulation techniques. This study can help in selecting the ZSI topology and suitable modulation technique for the voltage boost requirement demanded by the application.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control under Open-Circuit Fault in a 3-phase Open-end Winding Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The development of the aircrafts with electric and hybrid electric powertrain requires increase in reliability of the propulsion drives. One of the promising solution is the use of open-end winding machines and multiphase motors which are capable to produce the referenced torque in case of partial failures. This paper considers 3-phase open-end winding permanent magnet synchronous motor operated under open circuit fault. The use of model predictive control solves the problem of optimal current regulation as the cost function can minimize the ohmic losses together with delivering referenced torque to the propeller. The design of the control system for the faulty conditions is presented and simulation results shows that the model predictive control can be effectively used in such applications.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Asynchronous Fault Detection for Markov Jump Systems With Packet Loss Compensation and Partially Unknown Transition Probabilities
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper investigates the asynchronous fault detection (FD) problem for discrete-time interval type-2 (IT2) fuzzy Markov jump systems with packet loss compensation and partially unknown transition probabilities. To describe the asynchronous phenomenon that the mode information of the system cannot be communicated immediately to the filter, a hidden Markov model is utilized. Based on the single exponential smoothing method, an IT2 fuzzy FD filter is designed for generating a residual signal and detecting faults. Then, by employing Lyapunov theory, it is proved that the proposed FD filter ensures the stochastic stability and strict dissipativity of the filtering error system. Finally, a numerical example is given to verify the effectiveness of the proposed FD method.

articleTitle: Driving Cycle-Based Design and Optimization of Reduced Rare-Earth Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor for Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) is frequently employed as the propulsion motor for electric vehicles due to their high power density, good field weakening and speed regulation capabilities. Among the different rotor topologies, the double V-shaped configuration is one of the attractive alternatives when the power density needs to be enhanced. The volume of magnets is to be increased in order to achieve higher power density. However, conventional double V-shaped rotor employs only rare-earth magnets, which increases the overall cost of the motor. This work proposes a cost-effective double V-shaped rotor topology considering drive cycle-based design for electric vehicle applications. Variations of double V-shaped topology have been investigated aiming to lower the usage of rare-earth magnet. Multi-objective optimization has been performed to reduce rare earth magnet volume without compromising the power density. Cost estimation and simulation results as obtained from the 2D FEM environment have been presented.

Author Keywords: Reduced rare earth Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine

articleTitle: Predicting and Analyzing IoT Performance Based on Improved Resnet
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: With the increasing maturity of smart communication technologies and the rapid popularization of mobile IoT devices, technological development has gradually stepped into the world of the Internet of Everything, and the mobile Internet of Things (IoT) is booming, resulting in numerous applications of great significance. The complex and changing environment of mobile communication requires that mobile IoT applications can en-sure reliable delivery, more agile and accurate performance pre-diction methods are required. Outage probability (OP) is an important metric if one wants to evaluate the performance of mobile IoT networks. In this paper, we investigate the OP performance of mobile IoT communication networks based on an improved deep residual network (Resnet) and propose an prediction algorithm for OP based on the improved net-work. We first study the mobile OP performance and derive the accurate OP expression under a specific channel. Then, an improved residual network is designed to improve the prediction accuracy, the pooling layer of network is removed due to the characteristics of mobile communication data. The pro-posed prediction method based on improved residual network is compared with traditional convolutional neural network (CNN), generalized regression (GR) and radial basis function (RBF) methods. The simulation results verify that the proposed improved residual network prediction method can obtain better prediction results than the above traditional methods. The prediction accuracy of the Resnet method is improved by 44%.

articleTitle: Probability-Based Stealthy Attacks for Cyber-Physical Systems with Resource Constraint
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper focuses on designing resource-constrained stealthy attacks in linear Cyber-physical systems (CPS). The attacker’s primary objective is to maximize the disruption of the system’s performance while remaining undetected by detectors. In light of attack resource constraints, the attacker must also deliberate on the selection of target sensors to maximize the effectiveness of attacks. This paper presents the corresponding attack strategy, granting the attacker the flexibility to choose the specific sensors. Moreover, we formulate the optimization problem to determine the optimal attack strategy. Leveraging the Schur-Horn theorem, we successfully derive the optimal attack strategy and outline principles for the attacker in selecting sensor channels. Finally, the theoretical findings are validated through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Collaborative Object Detection and Distributed Fusion Based on Dual Camera
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This article investigates the collaborative localization and distributed fusion of multiple unmanned aerial vehicles based on cameras, including object detection algorithms, state estimation based on unscented Kalman filters(UKF), and data fusion. Starting from introducing the model we built in Gazebo and the 3D target localization implemented in real-time operating system(ROS), we analyzed the characteristics of the target detection results and the necessity for improvement. In order to obtain more accurate target positions, we proposed a collaborative localization algorithm based on post-fusion, which was processed and validated in MATLAB. Finally, the effectiveness of our algorithm was demonstrated through comparison.

articleTitle: Coordinated cyber attack of multiple step based on local and global information
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The coupling connection between power system and communication system enables smart grid evolve into cyber-physical power systems, reaching automatic operation in closed-loop. However, diverse hacker has imposed private attack on systems to steal information or implement sabotage. In this paper, the coupling connection between power system and communication system is analyzed, along with its interactive relation between nodes. Then, the requirement of survival sub-system and process of cascading failure are described in detail. Considering the local and global information, the coordinated attack of multiple step based on local and global information (adaptive attack) is proposed to effectively disintegrate the cyber-physical power systems. For various systems model, simulation has verified the effectiveness of attack methods on disintegrating systems.

articleTitle: Dynamic Coupling Characteristic Analysis of a Loaded Stewart Parallel Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The Stewart parallel robot always works with load and the load will cause dynamic coupling among different degree-of-freedoms, which seriously affects the accuracy of the system. In order to improve the accuracy and suppress the dynamic coupling, it is necessary to analyze the coupling characteristics of system dynamics. Aiming at the problem of dynamic coupling, this paper firstly established a dynamic modeling of the Stewart parallel robot with load, and then the dynamical coupling characteristics among the six degrees under the influence of the load are analyzed theoretically, and the reasons of the dynamic coupling and the distribution of dynamic coupling among six degrees are determined. Finally, a simulation was carried out in Simulink. The simulation results show that the dynamic coupling of the system is mainly caused by the load, and there are three types of dynamic coupling, and the dynamic coupling will change as the robot posture changes. The simulation results agree well with the theoretical analysis. Therefore, the research result in this paper can be used for the design of dynamic decoupling control strategy and system parameter identification algorithm.

articleTitle: Analysis of the peak and RMS current ratios in a dual active bridge converter with trapezoidal current modulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This research proposes a high-frequency isolation transformer (HFIT) (or inductor) current management ratios (CMRs) for a trapezoidal modulated dual active bridge (TraMDAB) converter suitable for automotive applications. The CMRs include peak-to-DC current (P2D) ratio recommended for managing HFIT saturation, RMS-to-DC current (R2D) ratio suitable for managing conduction loss, and peak-to-RMS current (P2R) ratio desirable when there is an objective to minimise both peak and RMS currents simultaneously. Firstly, explicit formulae for the inductor peak, inductor RMS, and the load currents are derived using the Faraday’s law of electromagnetic induction. From these, the CMRs were developed. The simulation results of a PLECS<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> based TraMDAB converter operated at different powers, the same powers and different operating regions show that power is more efficiently transferred at maximum power and when the input voltage is higher than the referred secondary voltage. However, power transfer at or close to the minimum power is recommended in case there is no choice than to transfer power when the input voltage is less than the referred secondary voltage.

articleTitle: A Novel Bidirectional High Gain DC-DC Converter with Active Switched Inductor and Wide Voltage Conversion Ratio
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Energy storage devices are indispensable for ensuring voltage and frequency stability in renewable energy sources such as solar and wind. Distributed generation systems necessitate bidirectional DC-DC converters to facilitate charge and discharge operations in accordance with operational requirements. In this paper, we introduce a new bidirectional DC-DC converter tailored to achieve substantial voltage gain while minimizing switch stress and maintaining a minimal component count. The proposed converter operates in buck mode for one power flow direction and boost mode for the other, ensuring continuous input and output current and reduced charging/discharging ripple. Comprehensive details regarding the derivation, operational principles, and meticulous steady-state analysis of the proposed converter are presented in this paper. Furthermore, a dynamic model of the converter is provided, and the design of closed-loop controllers for current control modes is outlined. We present extensive analysis and simulation results to illustrate the efficacy and performance of this novel topology. In summary, this converter offers a promising solution for achieving high-efficiency energy transfer with significant voltage gain, making it suitable for a wide array of applications.

articleTitle: Real-time Positioning and Mapping Based on Multi-sensor Fusion for Vehicle System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In the work, we propose a real-time positioning algorithm for vehicle state estimation during localization and mapping process. The method mainly relies on multi-sensor fusion and classical simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) technique. A factor map-based optimization framework is firstly designed which tightly couples the measurement produced by LiDAR, IMU and GNSS. New loopback constraints are further added to the back-end optimization problem thereby eliminating cumulative errors. Globally consistent trajectories and mapping results are finally obtained through the proposed method. We demonstrate its better real-time performance and higher localization accuracy compared with existing map-building algorithms by running the algorithm on a Jeston TX2 board.

articleTitle: Emitter Seed Localization using Movable Sensor Barriers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: We present a novel method for precise, non-optical 3D localization of a seed particle which emits a wave or particles which can be sensed by a detector and blocked by a barrier. A primary application of this method is the localization of radioactive seeds implanted into the body for cancer treatments. We have currently implemented an initial prototype demonstration system using an infrared LED as the emitter, photodetectors, and metal sheet barriers actuated by stepmotors to simulate radioactive seed localization. A geometric analysis of the concept is given and our prototype implementation is presented. Experimental results of the system demonstrate submillimeter localization accuracy.

articleTitle: Commandable areas of a Two-input three-level buck converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: An electrolyzer is a device which is used to produce hydrogen. This device requires a low voltage to operate. One way to reduce DC voltage is utilizing a two-input three-level buck converter. The challenge in controlling this type of converter is that sometimes the generated duty cycle located outside the interval between zero and one. Therefore, identifying the commandable areas for proper use of these converters is essential. In this article, by using the rules governing this converter and state equations, the commandable areas of the converter and its four switches have been identified by simulations results.

articleTitle: Improving Obstacle Avoidance Strategies in Autonomous Navigation of a Sailboat
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This work explores the different mechanisms involved in creating a behavioural system for route planning and collision avoidance, taking into account the constraints imposed by the navigational characteristics of the sailboat. The implementation of these mechanisms is accompanied by an introduction to fundamental concepts, including Artificial Potential Fields, Histograms of Vector Fields, Navigation in the No-Go Zone, Differentiation of the Nature of Obstacles resulting in Different Operations, and the Constitution of Different Areas of Actuation. Finally, multiple simulations are conducted in a virtual environment to verify the resilience of the proposed navigation strategy.

articleTitle: Non-Active Power Mitigation of Partial Power Processing DC-DC Converter for Onboard EV Charger
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper presents the Extended Phase Shift Control (EPSC) scheme of a DAB-based partial power processing converter for onboard electric vehicles (EVs) to mitigate the non-active power during charging. This converter can transfer the power in either direction in direct (lossless) and partial (lossy) paths. The partial path only comprises passive and active components, whereas no components are on the direct path. The active and non-active powers are associated with the partial path, and the direct path only transfers the active power. The Extended Phase Shift control scheme controls these powers. To verify the performance of the proposed partial converters with the control scheme, the converter Simulink model has been simulated and tested in the MATLAB environment. Under various operating conditions, their results are compared with the Single-Phase Shift (SPS) control scheme of partial and full-power converters. The results show that the proposed converter reduces up to 0.64KVAr to 1.4KVAr of non-active power compared with the Single-Phase Shift control scheme of partial and full-power converters during charging. Further, it is observed that the proposed converter achieves an efficiency of 97.8%, which is comparatively 3.5% higher than the Single-Phase Shift (SPS) control scheme of the partial converter and 12% higher than the full-power converters. Also, the partial path handles only 44% of output power. Therefore, the passive component power ratings and sizes can be significantly reduced. Hence, the proposed converter with the control scheme is more suitable for compact and highly efficient onboard EV charger design.

articleTitle: Path Planning of an Inchworm-like Robot in 3D Environment Based on Improved Ant Colony Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: To solve the global path planning of a 7-degree-of-freedom inchworm robot in a 3D hybrid environment of "pipe + wall", a planning method based on the A*-inspired ant colony algorithm is proposed. First of all, the coordinates of the reachable points are obtained by modelling the environment, and the set of reachable points is determined by combining with the workspace of the inchworm robot. Then, a heuristic function based on the A* algorithm is designed to improve the convergence speed of the algorithm; at the same time, a bending suppression operator is added to the heuristic function to reduce the problems of a large number of bending times and large cumulative bending angle caused by the A* algorithm. Finally, the maximum minimum ant system (MMAS) is introduced to solve the premature phenomenon that the traditional ACO algorithm may cause. The simulation results show that the method suits the three-dimensional environments of pure pipe, pure wall and "pipe+wall".

articleTitle: Short-Term Load Forecasting for Typical Buildings Based on VMD-Informer-DMD Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The accurate prediction of electric loads in typical buildings is essential for stable operation and efficient management of the power system. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel hybrid forecasting model that integrates data decomposition techniques, neural network models, and error correction techniques to predict short-term load. The variational mode decomposition (VMD) technique is used to reduce the complexity of signals by decomposing historical power load data into intrinsic mode functions of different frequencies. Then the attention mechanism and structural design of the Informer model are optimized to improve the accuracy of the model prediction. In the error correction stage, dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) is used to extract dynamic features of the error sequence and predict it for correction. Actual power load data is used in experimental analysis, demonstrating the proposed method’s higher accuracy.

articleTitle: Improving the Imperceptibility of Hidden Data in a Digital Image Using Difference Expansion
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The development in information technology has made digital images pervasive in many domains of work. To benefit the pervasiveness of the digital images, researchers use the pixels of the digital images to hide and carry secret data, known as steganography, confidentially. The existing works in steganography have shown weaknesses in conserving the quality of an image used to host the secret data when considering the large payloads. To mitigate this, this paper proposes a new steganographic scheme to improve the quality of the image carrying the secret data, evaluated as peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) quantified in decibels (dB) by using the expansion between the pixels in the neighbourhood in a customized manner. The experimentations, which yielded higher imperceptibility of the hidden data, have been done with random bits of secret data with sizes ranging from 1 to 100 kilobits. With our results, we obtained a PSNR of 62.478 dB, which is superior to the ones in the existing works.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Autonomous Underwater Vehicle Trajectory Tracking
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper develops a trajectory tracking control method for an autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) with four degrees of freedom (DOFs) using a Nonlinear Model Predictive Controller (NMPC). The NMPC is implemented for a nonlinear AUV system and an advanced CasADi framework is applied to accomplish the nonlinear optimization required in the control strategy. Simulations are conducted to verify the tracking effectiveness of the proposed control algorithm, where satisfactory accuracy and efficiency are performed even with physical constraints and environmental disturbances involved, thus guaranteeing the robustness of the method.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Performance Analysis of Steel-Canned Halbach Permanent Magnet Rotor Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) presented in this paper consists of a new Steel-Canned Halbach Permanent Magnet (SCHPM) rotor, which provides a significant reduction in the total harmonic distortion of the air-gap flux and torque ripple of the machine. The proposed rotor consists of a two-segment Halbach PM array which is enclosed within a solid steel-can. The magnetic equivalent circuit (MEC) model is derived for analytical estimation of the magnetic flux density in the air-gap due to the rotor. The dimensions of the magnets and the thickness of the steel-can in the SCHPM rotor are obtained through parametric simulation using finite element analysis (FEA). The electromagnetic performance of the proposed machine is also analyzed using FEA to validate the air-gap flux density calculation from the MEC model. Finally, a three-phase, 30 kW, 10-pole PMSM is designed for the proposed rotor structure. The electromagnetic performance of the machine is analyzed using FEA and compared with the surface mount Halbach PMSM (SHPMSM) of the same power rating. It is found that the peak-to-peak torque ripple, core loss, and magnet loss are reduced by 32.6%, 7.03%, and 44.6%.

articleTitle: General Research and Design of Snake Robot for Fault Detection in Confined Space*
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this paper, the current research status of snake robots at home and abroad is firstly investigated, followed by its key technologies, and finally a design solution suitable for confined space and radiation resistance is proposed.

articleTitle: Active and Reactive Power Sharing of Two Parallel Inverters Using Combination of Virtual Synchronous Generator and Droop Control.
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 2nd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The concept of active, reactive, and harmonic distortion powers sharing of two inverters connected in parallel to the main grid becomes a very important problem for security of supply. The first contribution presented in the paper is the combination of a virtual synchronous generator (VSG) and a nonlinear current control technique.
